research.area: USGS EarthExplorer and the M2M API for declassified satellite imagery (Corona/Argon/Lanyard, KH-7 Gambit, KH-9 Hexagon), as of 2026-10-11
research.summary: Scope note: the user said they will not use fostulbucuresti resources and will buy their own imagery from USGS. Everything below assumes that path: free downloads of frames USGS has already scanned, plus paid scan-on-demand for frames that have not been scanned yet. Live checks (curl, 2026-10-11, no credentials): - The base URL https://m2m.cr.usgs.gov/api/api/json/stable/ is live. - The password `login` endpoint now returns `NOT_FOUND "Invalid Endpoint"`. It was announced for deprecation on 2025-02-26 and is gone. `login-token` works: `{}` returns "The parameter username is required". - Version paths `/1.5/` and `/2.0/` return `VERSION_UNKNOWN`. Only `stable` and `development` resolve. - The M2M docs (/api/docs/json/), the test page and the examples now redirect to an ERS login, so the official reference is no longer publicly readable. I had to rebuild endpoint details from USGS PDFs, USGS help pages and open-source clients that copy the official docstrings. - Unauthenticated or invalid-token calls to data endpoints return an HTML 403 page, not JSON. CORS (tested live): - The M2M API echoes Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for *.usgs.gov origins (earthexplorer.usgs.gov, m2m.cr.usgs.gov, ers.cr.usgs.gov, even a made-up foo.usgs.gov). - It sends no ACAO for https://ventura8.github.io, localhost or null, on both the OPTIONS preflight and the actual responses. - So a github.io admin page cannot call M2M directly. A server-side hop is required (GitHub Actions, or a Cloudflare Worker or similar proxy). Firebase Functions would need Blaze, which this account doesn't have. - Browse JPEGs on ims.cr.usgs.gov download without auth (HTTP 200, cached for 1 year) but carry no CORS headers. They work in an `` tag but cannot be loaded as a Mapbox GL image source or WebGL texture without a proxy or a copy. Dataset names (confirmed from a real 2026-07 harvest by an open-source project, the kapadia/usgs catalog, spymicmac and the TAO plugin): - Declass 1 (Corona KH-1 to KH-4B, Argon KH-5, Lanyard KH-6, 1960-72) = `corona2` - Declass 2 (KH-7 Gambit high-res 'H' and KH-9 lower-res mapping camera 'L', 1963-80) = `declassii` - Declass 3 (KH-9 Hexagon panoramic, A = aft, F = forward, 1971-84) = `declassiii` - `declassi` appears in one third-party script but is not a valid alias; that project's own harvest found only the three above after 'hardcoded aliases proved wrong: DATASET_INVALID'. - To discover aliases: POST dataset-search with `{"datasetName":"declass"}` or `{"datasetName":"corona"}` (wildcard match) and read `datasetAlias`. Authentication: - Request M2M access on your ERS profile ('Request Access' → M2M API option). USGS reviews requests within 24-48 business hours. - Generate an application token in ERS (Profile → Application Tokens): - Optional expiry date; no date means it never expires. - Scope it to 'M2M API'. - Up to 10 tokens per user, revocable at any time. - It is shown only for 60 seconds. - Not affected by password expiry. - POST login-token `{username, token}` returns `data` = API key. Send it as the `X-Auth-Token` header on all other calls. - The API key is valid for 2 hours. Per the official docstring copied into clients, call `logout` when done. - download-options, download-request, order-products and rate-limit-summary need the M2M ('MACHINE') role. - ERS added an optional MFA passkey login (planned release 2025-09-29). Application tokens are the headless path. Pricing and ordering (USGS pages): - Downloading frames that are already scanned is free ("download existing digital files at no cost"). - A frame that has not been scanned can be ordered for on-demand scanning at 7 µm (3600 dpi) or 14 µm (1800 dpi); colour is 14 µm only. - Price: $30 per frame/scene plus a $5 handling/order fee per request. This is non-refundable and first-in-first-out, with no priority service. - You order through the EarthExplorer UI (basket icon → Item Basket → On-Demand). USGS/Reston (Business Partner Office) then contacts you to take payment by credit card. Unpaid requests are deleted after 2 weeks. - Turnaround is quoted as 3-4 weeks after payment (one EE help answer says 2-3 weeks). - After scanning, the frame is archived and downloadable through EE at no cost. - I found no 2024-2026 notice of a price change. The newest page that states the price is dated 2024-05-15. It is not free. - One open-source project's handbook (2026) says 'order a free scan-on-demand', but that contradicts every USGS page and is not credible. Ordering via M2M: - M2M has order-products, order-submit and dataset-order-products endpoints. order-submit 'Submits the current product list as a TRAM order'. - I found no evidence anyone has used them to place a paid declass scan order. One 2026 project lists 'try M2M ordering endpoints, fall back to manual EE ordering' as unfinished backlog. - Treat ordering and payment as a manual EE step done by the user. Automate everything around it: discovery, cost estimate, then polling download-options until `available` flips to true, then download. Download flow: 1. download-options `{datasetName, entityIds}` lists products with `id`, `productCode`, `productName` (e.g. 'Standard Format' for corona2), `available`, `filesize`. 2. download-request `{downloads:[{entityId, productId}], label}` returns `availableDownloads[].url`, `preparingDownloads`, `failed`, `duplicateProducts`, `newRecords`, `remainingLimits`. 3. Poll download-retrieve `{label}` until the item appears under `available` with a `url`. 4. GET the URL. It is a signed URL; existing clients fetch it without auth headers. 5. Clean up with download-order-remove / download-remove. What a download contains: - The product is an archive (.tgz/.tar.gz, extracted by both open-source pipelines) holding the film scan in several overlapping TIFF segments (`_a.tif`, `_b.tif`, ...). The frame is not georeferenced. - USGS size guidance: - Corona: 4 × 80 MB at 14 µm, or 4 × 319 MB at 7 µm. - KH-7: about 1 GB per file at 7 µm. - KH-9 mapping camera: 2 × 1 GB at 7 µm. One real 2026 example was 2 × 1.28 GB. - KH-9 panoramic (Declass 3): 725 MB per file at 7 µm for 6.5-inch film, with a variable number of files. - Plan for 1-5+ GB per scene. Metadata: - scene-search results have entityId, displayId, `browse[]` (browsePath, thumbnailPath, overlayPath), spatialBounds, spatialCoverage, temporalCoverage{startDate,endDate}, `options{bulk,download,order,secondary}` and `metadata[]` ({id, fieldName, dictionaryLink, value}) when metadataType='full'. - Declass field names: 'Entity ID', 'Acquisition Date' (YYYY/MM/DD), 'Mission' / 'Mission Number', 'Frame' / 'Frame Number', 'Camera' / 'Camera Type', 'Camera Resolution', 'Film Type', 'Generation', 'Polarity', 'Download Available' (Y/N, or 0/1 in some exports), 'Image Preview Availability'. - Corners: 'NW Corner Lat dec', 'NW Corner Long dec' and the same for NE, SE, SW, plus 'Center Latitude dec' / 'Center Longitude dec', and DMS variants without ' dec'. Some records spell it 'NW Cormer Lat dec'. Practical lessons from a similar 2026 open-source project (Syria explorer, MIT): archive corner coordinates are often far off (up to about 35 km RMS), and frames can come rotated or mirrored, so corner-based georeferencing is only a first pass before GCP or human alignment. M2M also has maintenance windows (Tuesdays) that return 503 HTML, so retry.

research.concrete_details:
BASE: https://m2m.cr.usgs.gov/api/api/json/stable/<endpoint>. Always POST with Content-Type: application/json. Header X-Auth-Token: <apiKey> on every call after login.
Response envelope: {requestId, version, data, errorCode, errorMessage}. On errors you can also get non-JSON HTML (403 for missing/invalid auth; 503 'Application Offline' during maintenance), so parse defensively and retry.

AUTH
- POST login-token {"username":"<ERS user>","token":"<app token>"} → {data:"<apiKey>"}. The key lasts 2 h.
- POST logout {} when done.
- Get the token from ERS https://ers.cr.usgs.gov/ → Profile → Application Tokens → Create (scope 'M2M API', optional expiry, max 10 tokens, copy it within 60 s).
- Request access: ERS profile → Request Access → M2M API (approval takes 24-48 business hours).
- Password `login` → NOT_FOUND (removed after 2025-02-26).
- Other endpoints that exist: login-sso, login-app-guest.

DATASET DISCOVERY
- POST dataset-search {"datasetName":"declass"} (wildcard). Read data[].datasetAlias and collectionName.
- Expected aliases: corona2, declassii, declassiii.
- POST dataset-filters {"datasetName":"declassii"} → filterId per field (e.g. Camera filterId 5e839ff8cfa94807 in declassii, per the usgsxplore README). Use these for metadataFilter.

SCENE SEARCH (Bucharest bbox ≈ lon 25.95-26.25, lat 44.33-44.55)
POST scene-search
{"datasetName":"declassiii",
 "maxResults":1000, "startingNumber":1,
 "metadataType":"full",
 "sceneFilter":{
   "spatialFilter":{"filterType":"mbr",
     "lowerLeft":{"latitude":44.33,"longitude":25.95},
     "upperRight":{"latitude":44.55,"longitude":26.25}},
   "acquisitionFilter":{"start":"1960-01-01","end":"1984-12-31"},
   "metadataFilter":{"filterType":"value","filterId":"<id from dataset-filters>","value":"Y","operand":"="}}}

- Alternative spatialFilter: {"filterType":"geojson","geoJson":{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[lon,lat],...]]}}.
- metadataFilter combinators: {"filterType":"and"|"or","childFilters":[...]}, {"filterType":"between","filterId","firstValue","secondValue"}.
- Other sceneFilter keys: cloudCoverFilter{min,max,includeUnknown}, ingestFilter{start,end}, seasonalFilter[months].
- `temporalFilter` belongs to dataset-search, not scene-search.
- Response data: {results[], recordsReturned, totalHits, totalHitsAccuracy, startingNumber, nextRecord, numExcluded, isCustomized}.
- Each result: entityId, displayId, orderingId, publishDate, temporalCoverage{startDate,endDate}, spatialBounds, spatialCoverage (GeoJSON), options{bulk,download,order,secondary}, selected{bulk,compare,order}, metadata[{id,fieldName,dictionaryLink,value}], browse[{id,browseName,browsePath,thumbnailPath,overlayPath,overlayType,browseRotationEnabled}].
- Limit: 50,000 results per search.

SCENE METADATA
- POST scene-metadata {"datasetName","entityId","metadataType":"full"} (idType can be entityId|displayId|orderingId).
- Batch alternative: scene-list-add {listId, datasetName, entityIds, timeToLive:"PT1M"} + scene-metadata-list {listId, datasetName, metadataType:"full"}.
- Declass fieldName values:
  - Identity and acquisition: 'Entity ID', 'Acquisition Date' (YYYY/MM/DD), 'Mission' / 'Mission Number', 'Frame' / 'Frame Number', 'Camera' / 'Camera Type', 'Camera Resolution', 'Film Type', 'Generation', 'Polarity', 'Image Type', 'Operations Number', 'Segment Count' (declassii), 'Download Available', 'Image Preview Availability'.
  - Coordinates: 'Center Latitude dec', 'Center Longitude dec', 'NW Corner Lat dec', 'NW Corner Long dec', 'NE Corner Lat dec', 'NE Corner Long dec', 'SE Corner Lat dec', 'SE Corner Long dec', 'SW Corner Lat dec', 'SW Corner Long dec' (DMS versions drop ' dec'). Watch for the 'Cormer' typo.
- Entity ID patterns:
  - Corona: DS1038-1006DA033 or DS009013039DV181.
  - KH-7: DZB00402700090H020001.
  - KH-9 mapping camera: DZB1214-500347L001001.
  - KH-9 panoramic: D3C1219-100204A001.
- Browse URL patterns (public, cache 1 yr, no CORS):
  - corona2: https://ims.cr.usgs.gov/browse/DIT/9013/039D/V/DS009013039DV181.jpg (28 KB)
  - declassii: https://ims.cr.usgs.gov/browse/declassii/004001/00009/DZB00400100009H010015-01149.jpg (1.3 MB)
  - declassiii: https://ims.cr.usgs.gov/browse/declass3/1201-1/00012/A/D3C1201-100012A001.jpg (4.5 MB)
  - Thumbnails: replace /browse/ with /thumbnail/.

DOWNLOAD (needs MACHINE role)
1. POST download-options {"datasetName","entityIds":["..."] or "id1,id2"} → [{id, entityId, productCode, productName (corona2: 'Standard Format'), available (bool), filesize, bulkAvailable, downloadSystem, secondaryDownloads}].
2. POST download-request {"downloads":[{"entityId","productId":<option.id>}],"label":"<unique>"} → {availableDownloads[{downloadId,entityId,url}], preparingDownloads[], failed[], newRecords{}, duplicateProducts{}, numInvalidScenes, remainingLimits[{limitType:'user'|'ip', recentDownloadCount, pendingDownloadCount, unattemptedDownloadCount}]}.
3. If preparing: poll POST download-retrieve {"label"} every ~30 s → {available[{downloadId,entityId,url,filesize,...}], requested[], queueSize, eulas}.
4. GET the url (no auth header; signed) and read the filename from Content-Disposition.
5. Clean up: download-order-remove {label}, download-search {label|activeOnly}, download-remove {downloadId}.
- Monitoring: rate-limit-summary {} → initialLimits / remainingLimits / recentDownloadCounts (15-minute window, per user and per IP). Error code RATE_LIMIT or HTTP 429 → back off.
- Archive contents: .tgz/.tar.gz of <entityId>_a.tif, _b.tif, … (overlapping segments, ungeoreferenced). Mosaic the segments (gdalbuildvrt or offset matching) → GCPs → gdalwarp → tiles.
- Sizes: Corona 4×80 MB @14 µm or 4×319 MB @7 µm; KH-7 1 GB/file @7 µm (780 MB colour @14 µm); KH-9 mapping 2×1 GB @7 µm; KH-9 panoramic 725 MB/file (6.5-inch film) or 1 GB/file (9-inch) @7 µm, several files per frame.

ORDERING (scan-on-demand)
- Price: $30 per frame plus $5 per order.
- Steps: EarthExplorer UI (https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov) → results with the basket icon → Item Basket → On-Demand → choose 7 or 14 µm → submit → USGS Business Partner Office invoices or calls for a credit card → wait 3-4 weeks.
- Unpaid orders are deleted after 2 weeks. Reactivate via GS-A-HQ_RMS@usgs.gov. Support: custserv@usgs.gov, 1-800-252-4547.
- M2M endpoints exist but are unverified for paid declass orders: dataset-order-products {datasetName}, order-products {datasetName, entityIds|listId} (returns price and availability), order-submit {products[], orderComment, ...} (TRAM order).

OPEN-SOURCE CLIENTS
- usgsxplore (pip install usgsxplore; v1.1.5, 2026-09-11, MIT; env vars USGS_USERNAME / USGS_TOKEN; uses login-token):
  - `usgsxplore search declassiii -b 25.95 44.33 26.25 44.55 -f "DOWNLOAD_AVAILABLE=Y" -o r.gpkg -o r.txt`
  - `usgsxplore download r.txt -o ./data` (extracts .tgz automatically)
  - `usgsxplore download-browse r.gpkg` (GeoTIFF browse placed from the 4 corner GCPs)
  - `usgsxplore info filters declassii`
- callusgs v0.3.0 (2025-01): Python, covers nearly every endpoint, including order-submit and rate-limit-summary.
- usgsm2m (R, 2026).
- Node scripts to copy for a JS GitHub Action (MIT): Triavision-ai/historical-syria-explorer scripts/find-digitized.mjs, download-declass.mjs, harvest-declass.mjs, prepare-frame.mjs, and workflow tile-declass-scene.yml (ubuntu-latest + apt gdal-bin, timeout 330 min).
- landsatxplore still uses the removed password login, so avoid it.
research.risks_and_unknowns:
1. The official M2M reference (/api/docs/json/, /api/docs/reference/, /api/test/json/) is now behind an ERS login, so I could not read it directly. Endpoint shapes come from USGS PDFs and help pages plus several independent clients that copy the official docstrings. Once the M2M role is granted, check them on the logged-in docs page.
2. Paying for a scan through M2M (order-submit) is unverified and probably unsupported for declass. Assume payment is a manual EarthExplorer + credit-card step the user does personally; Claude must not do purchases. To check: after approval, call dataset-order-products for corona2, declassii and declassiii, and order-products for one unscanned entityId, and see whether a price or product appears.
3. Fee currency: the newest USGS page that states $30/frame + $5/order is dated 2024-05-15. There is no 2025-2026 confirmation and the EE checkout may show different numbers. Confirm on the EE checkout or by emailing custserv@usgs.gov before budgeting. Turnaround figures vary (2-3 or 3-4 weeks after payment).
4. Which resolution an already-scanned frame comes at (7 vs 14 µm), and the exact productName/productCode for declassii and declassiii, are not documented. Read them from download-options per scene. The archive type (.tgz vs .tar) also varies, so handle both.
5. Rate-limit numbers are not published; read rate-limit-summary at runtime. Limits are per user and per IP, and GitHub-hosted runner IPs are shared, so an IP limit could hit sooner than expected (inference).
6. CORS was tested by curl on 2026-10-11 against the Origin allowlist. USGS could change it, but the code should assume there is no browser access.
   - To re-verify in a browser on github.io, run in the console: fetch('https://m2m.cr.usgs.gov/api/api/json/stable/login-token',{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:'{}'}). Expect a CORS error.
   - With curl: `curl -i -X OPTIONS <url> -H 'Origin: https://ventura8.github.io' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST'` and look for Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
7. Browse JPEGs have no CORS. Overlaying them in Mapbox requires copying them via an Action into your own storage or Mapbox, or a third-party proxy (wsrv.nl), which adds a dependency.
8. Bucharest coverage and how much of it is already scanned are unknown until you run an authenticated search. Declass-3 ingestion was still 'ongoing' on the USGS page (over 670k scenes), so some KH-9 panoramic frames may not be in the catalog yet.
9. Georeferencing accuracy: archive corners can be off by kilometres, and frames can be rotated or mirrored. Panoramic Corona and KH-9 frames have strong panoramic distortion, so an affine fit from 4 corners is insufficient for street-level overlays. You need many GCPs or polynomial/TPS warps, plus human checking.
10. Raster size: 1-5+ GB per scene, more after mosaic and warp. Check GitHub-hosted runner disk space (about 14 GB free by default unless you clean up) and the 6-hour job limit. Also check Mapbox upload limits for large GeoTIFFs (not researched here).
11. ERS MFA passkey (2025): app tokens are documented as unaffected by password/profile changes, but any future ERS policy change could hit headless use. Store the token as a GitHub Actions secret and set an expiry reminder; another project's token silently expired on 2026-07-31.
12. 'Download Available' appears as Y/N in filters but 0/1 in some metadata exports. Normalize it.

verified.claim: 1. The M2M base URL is https://m2m.cr.usgs.gov/api/api/json/stable/. Calls are POST with JSON bodies, and auth uses the X-Auth-Token header.
verified.correction: Correct. Live probes on 2026-10-11: 'stable' and 'development' resolve and '/1.5/' returns VERSION_UNKNOWN. The official reference pages (/api/docs/json/, /docs/reference/, /docs/datadictionary/) now return a 302 to the M2M login page, so the reference is not publicly readable. Detail the researcher missed: JSON errors come back with HTTP status 500 (login-token with {} returned HTTP 500 with errorCode INPUT_PARAMETER_REQUIRED). The USGS sample script says '500 errors mean there is an error but it may have been caught'. Clients must parse the body on any status code.

verified.claim: 2. The password 'login' endpoint was announced for deprecation on 2025-02-26 and now returns NOT_FOUND 'Invalid Endpoint'. login-token is the working programmatic login.
verified.correction: Live result: POST /stable/login returns {errorCode:'NOT_FOUND', errorMessage:'Invalid Endpoint'}, and login-token with {} returns 'The parameter username is required'. login-sso and login-app-guest also exist: live, they return AUTH_ERROR 'No Valid Identity Detected' and 'parameter applicationToken is required'. login-sso relies on an ERS SSO cookie, and login-app-guest needs a USGS-issued application token. Neither is usable from github.io. login-token is the only practical headless path.

verified.claim: 3. Application tokens: created in the ERS profile, optional expiry (none means it never expires), scope 'M2M API', at most 10 per user, revocable, shown for only 60 s, not affected by password expiry.
verified.correction: Every point matches the PDF text, which says: 'up to 10 of these tokens', 'if not provided, the token does not expire', 'cleared from the screen after 60 seconds', and 'not impacted by password expiration or profile update requirements'. The PDF page footer reads 072024.

verified.claim: 4. M2M access is requested in ERS ('Request Access' → M2M API) and reviewed within 24-48 business hours. Download endpoints need the MACHINE role.
verified.correction: The USGS FAQ (updated 2026-03-31) says 'Requests are reviewed within 24 to 48 business hours.' The MACHINE-role requirement comes from official docstrings copied into callusgs, not from a public USGS page. callusgs also says scene search and scene lists work WITHOUT the MACHINE role, so discovery may work before download approval. I could not confirm whether login-token itself needs approval first. The usgsxplore README says to request access at ers.cr.usgs.gov/profile/access and 'specify the datasets you plan to use'.

verified.claim: 5. CORS: M2M echoes Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for *.usgs.gov origins and sends none for https://ventura8.github.io, so browser calls from github.io are blocked.
verified.correction: Reproduced live. The OPTIONS preflight returns 204 with Allow-Credentials, Allow-Headers (including X-Auth-Token) and Allow-Methods, but no ACAO for github.io or localhost. earthexplorer.usgs.gov and the made-up foo.usgs.gov get ACAO echoed. The same holds on the POST response. A server-side hop is required.

verified.correction: Live: all three example URLs return 200 with Cache-Control max-age=31536000 and no ACAO. Sizes are 28,228 B, 1,288,080 B and 4,462,195 B, matching the researcher's figures. wsrv.nl returns 'access-control-allow-origin: *' for the same image. It is a free third-party proxy, so it is a dependency risk.

verified.claim: 7. Dataset aliases: corona2 = Declass 1, declassii = Declass 2 (KH-7 plus KH-9 mapping camera), declassiii = Declass 3 (KH-9 panoramic).
verified.correction: Harvest counts confirmed: generatedAt 2026-07-21T18:28:59Z, corona2 4855, declassiii 3452, declassii 257. The harvest script says 'hardcoded aliases proved wrong: DATASET_INVALID', and find-digitized.mjs in the same repo still hardcodes the invalid 'declassi'. verified.claim: 8. The 'Download Available' metadata field shows whether a frame is already scanned. download-options 'available' is the operational check.
verified.correction: The official Declass 3 data dictionary defines it as indicating 'if an image has already been scanned and is available for immediate download'. verified.claim: 9. Corner field names are 'NW Corner Lat dec', 'NW Corner Long dec' (and NE/SE/SW), 'Center Latitude dec' and 'Center Longitude dec', plus DMS variants without ' dec'. Some records spell it 'NW Cormer Lat dec'.

verified.claim: 11. No 2024-2026 USGS notice changes the $30 fee. Scanning is not free, and the third-party 'free scan-on-demand' line is wrong.

verified.claim: 14. Download flow: download-options → download-request → poll download-retrieve(label) → GET the signed URL without an auth header. The archive holds <entityId>_a.tif, _b.tif, and so on.

verified.claim: 15. Sizes: Corona 4×80 MB at 14 µm or 4×319 MB at 7 µm; KH-7 about 1 GB per file at 7 µm; KH-9 mapping 2×1 GB at 7 µm (real example 2×1.28 GB); KH-9 panoramic 725 MB per file (6.5-inch, 7 µm), several files.

The KH-7 file count varies with image length. Declass 3 at 14 µm is 188 MB (6.5-inch) or 260 MB (9-inch), and 9-inch at 7 µm is 1 GB. verified.correction: This is a practitioner report, not USGS documentation. The 35 km figure was the WORST case seen (the Raqqa strip), not typical. The report also says frames can be rotated about 48-118° and MIRRORED, and two-point similarity checks cannot detect mirroring.

verified.claim: M2M has maintenance windows on Tuesdays that return 503 HTML.

research.area: Automating georeferencing of USGS declassified imagery (Corona KH-4A/KH-4B, KH-9 Hexagon panoramic and mapping camera, KH-7) for Bucharest (~44.43N 26.10E): acquiring scans from USGS, stitching, generating GCPs, warping with GDAL, publishing a GeoTIFF/COG sized for Mapbox, and browser UX for refining GCPs.
research.summary:
CONTEXT CHECK (read-only look at the repo). The current site's index.html uses Mapbox tilesets from the fostulbucuresti account: "Corona (KH-4A), High Resolution, 1966, USGS" (6 tilesets, maxzoom 18), "KH-9 Hexagon, High Resolution" for 1976 (3 tilesets), 1977 (2) and 1980 (3), and "KH-9 Hexagon, Low Resolution Mapping, 1978" (1 tileset, maxzoom 15). It also loads Mapbox GL JS v2.6.1. Per the user's instruction we will not reuse any of these. What they do show is that USGS frames covering Bucharest exist for KH-4A in 1966, KH-9 panoramic in 1976/77/80 and KH-9 mapping camera in 1978. Splitting each year into several tilesets suggests the previous author warped each scan segment or frame separately (my inference).

BUYING FROM USGS (verified). EarthExplorer offers two scan resolutions, 7 µm (3600 dpi) and 14 µm (1800 dpi). Frames that are already scanned download for free. Frames not yet scanned need an on-demand scan order at $30 per frame (USGS Declass-1/2/3 pages). A USGS FAQ (seen only as a search snippet) adds a $5 order fee and a 3-4 week turnaround with no priority option, and says orders must be placed in the EarthExplorer UI. A 2018 USGS article says scanned frames are then posted on EarthExplorer "free of charge" for everyone, so a paid scan is not exclusive to us. USGS-produced data is public domain; USGS asks for a credit line such as "... courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey". For scripted downloads, the M2M API's password 'login' endpoint was scheduled for deprecation on 2025-02-26 and replaced by 'login-token' with an application token. Dataset names used by third-party clients are corona2 (Declass 1) and declassii (Declass 2); I could not confirm the Declass 3 name. The Declass-3 data dictionary includes a "Download Available" flag, a "High Resolution Download Available" (orderable) flag, camera mode A/F/T, and NE/NW/SE/SW corner coordinates. Declass-3 metadata says its holdings are "primarily over the United States, Antarctica, and the Arctic Circle". The old site's 1976-80 KH-9 high-res layers suggest Bucharest is covered anyway, but this must be checked in EarthExplorer.

1) WHAT GEOREFERENCE INFO USGS PROVIDES. Each scene has only NW/NE/SE/SW corners plus a center point, calculated from camera operation and the satellite's path. USGS says the scans are not georeferenced and no geocorrection is applied. The CoSP paper (arXiv 2201.07756) measured the corner error: corners "can deviate several kilometers from their real positions in a typical scenario or up to 100 km in certain cases". Corners are therefore only good for finding the search window.

Scans arrive in parts:
- Corona film (70 mm x 29.8 in) comes as 4 overlapping TIFFs, _a to _d: about 80 MB each at 14 µm and 319 MB each at 7 µm.
- KH-9 mapping camera (9x18 in) comes as 2 halves, about 1 GB each at 7 µm.
- KH-7 and KH-9 panoramic come in a variable number of overlapping sections (KH-7 in 9.5-inch sections, about 1 GB per file at 7 µm; Declass-3 6.5-inch film about 725 MB per file at 7 µm).

Stitching approaches:
- ASP's image_mosaic matches interest points in the overlap with RANSAC and fits rotation+translation, or affine with --use-affine-transform. The ASP KH-4B example feeds the parts in reverse order (d c b a) with --overlap-width 7000 --blend-radius 2000, and adds --rotate (180°) for aft-camera frames.
- spymicmac's join_hexagon searches a 2000 px overlap by default and can blend linearly. Its docs say 'a' is the left part.
- CoSP stitches a+b and c+d first, then merges the two halves, each with a rigid transform.
- The CORONA Atlas stitched with SIFT (VLFeat).
Part order and orientation have to be checked per frame (forward vs aft camera) and must not be hard-coded.

2) QUALITY OF A SIMPLE 4-CORNER WARP. A warp from the metadata corners is wrong by kilometres (verified). Literature on whole-frame or large-area polynomial and rubber-sheet fits of KH-4B reports errors of 100 m or more even on flat terrain (Internet Archaeology / CORONA Atlas). The CORONA Atlas reports that its rigorous panoramic model gives 3-10 m at nadir and 20-80 m at frame edges. 2OC (Remote Sensing 2023) reports better than 4 m at checkpoints and says SIFT/SURF are unstable on Corona. CoSP reports about 2 px with a rigorous model, and residuals from film deformation of up to about 6 px.

My own geometric derivation (inference) for a city-sized window of about 24x23 km cut from the 188-218 km long panoramic scan:
- Ground position along the scan follows H·tan(θ).
- Near nadir, the error left after a best-fit linear (affine/projective) model is only a few metres.
- At about 30° off-nadir, the quadratic term leaves about 100-150 m after a linear fit. A 2nd-order polynomial or TPS removes most of it.
- Relief displacement in Bucharest (about 40 m of relief) is up to about 20 m at 30° off-nadir.

Expected accuracy of 4 well-placed GCPs with a projective model on the city crop (inference):
- KH-9 mapping camera (a frame camera with a réseau grid): about 1-3 px, i.e. 10-30 m.
- KH-4A/4B: about 5-20 m if Bucharest is near the scan centre, 50-150+ m if near the scan ends.
- KH-9 panoramic (f = 1.5 m, scan up to 120°) and KH-7 (strip camera): worse in pixel terms, so they need dense GCPs.

With 30-100+ well-spread, cleaned GCPs and TPS or a polynomial of order 2-3 on the crop, about 1-3 px of effective resolution is realistic: roughly 3-10 m for Corona and 1-3 m for KH-9 panoramic (inference). Supporting data points: a 2025 IEEE JSTARS paper reports 5.99 m mean absolute error for CORONA (method not stated in the abstract), and the Hungarian national Corona mosaic used 40-170 GCPs per image with Delaunay triangulation. TPS passes exactly through every GCP, so accuracy must be measured on held-out checkpoints.

3) AUTOMATIC REFINEMENT. Feasible, but needs a coarse-to-fine design and a human QA step.
- Evidence that learned matchers work: CoSP used SuperGlue against a 3 m PlanetScope mosaic, or 15 m Landsat panchromatic, with coarse-to-fine tiling (1920x1440 patches). It got no matches in forested or changed areas.
- DLR's 2026 AerialRefMatch benchmark (ISPRS Annals XI-2-2026) found fewer than 14% of raw aerial images could be oriented to pixel accuracy. With approximate pre-orthorectification, up to 30% succeeded (JamMa, SIFT, SuperPoint+LightGlue). ELoFTR and RoMa were more robust on raw images but less precise.
- Lesson: pre-rectify first, then match finely.
- AROSICS (v1.13.2, Oct 2025) does Fourier-domain local co-registration on a tie-point grid. Defaults are window 256 px, max_shift 5 px and RANSAC filtering, and the tie points can be exported (CoRegPoints_table, GCPList). Its own docs say both images must already be roughly geocoded and orthorectified, so it suits only the final sub-pixel to few-pixel refinement step.
- Full photogrammetric tools are heavy and stereo/DEM-oriented, so they are overkill for one 2D city crop: spymicmac (MicMac has no optical-bar camera, so panoramic needs ASP), HEXIMAP (MATLAB, KH-9 mapping camera only), and ASP cam_gen opticalbar + bundle_adjust/jitter_solve.

Urban change from the 1960s to today (my inference): matching will work on persistent structures (major boulevards, rail lines, lakes, parks, the old street grid). It will fail where large areas were rebuilt, such as the 1980s Civic Centre and the new housing estates. That calls for robust outlier rejection plus manual review.

Reference imagery licensing (flag):
- Mapbox tile terms (2021 copy) forbid deriving or extracting data from map tiles, including satellite imagery, "for any purpose". The OSM exception exists only in a third-party post.
- Esri World Imagery is under the Esri Master License Agreement and is not intended for export.
- The Copernicus VHR 2021 2 m mosaic is WMS view-only with unclear terms.
- The ANCPI orthophoto WMS has restricted access with tariffs.
- Sentinel-2 L2A COGs (Earth Search collection sentinel-2-c1-l2a, no auth) are open, but at 10 m they are only good for coarse GCPs (about 5-15 m).

4) PIPELINE. Use GDAL ≥3.11 from the official container ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-3.13.3. Ubuntu 24.04's apt GDAL is older; that is my assumption and was not checked. GDAL 3.11 added a homography GCP transformer: gdalwarp picks it automatically for 4-5 GCPs, or it can be forced with -to SRC_METHOD=GCP_HOMOGRAPHY. With more than 6 GCPs the default is a 2nd-order polynomial. -tps forces thin-plate spline, which needs RAM of at least N²·8 bytes. Steps: crop early → optional per-segment georeferencing instead of stitching → GCPs → gdalwarp -tps to EPSG:3857 on a tile-aligned bbox → 8-bit output for Mapbox (Mapbox says only 8-bit GeoTIFF, 10 GB limit via the Uploads API, 300 MB in the Studio UI, 256x256 blocks, LZW) plus a JPEG/DEFLATE COG for archive and preview. Full commands are in concrete_details.

5) RESOURCES (inference from USGS file sizes). A KH-4A/B scene at 7 µm is about 1.3 GB to download. A Bucharest crop is about 150-300 MB, and warped output is about 0.2-0.8 Gpx. The free public-repo ubuntu-latest runner (4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD, 6 h per job; verified) handles this with a large margin. KH-9 panoramic/KH-7 scenes can be several GB; keep them small on disk by streaming through tar and keeping only the needed members, using /vsitar/, and freeing disk (jlumbroso/free-disk-space claims up to 31 GB).

6) UX. Use a MapWarper-style split view: raw-scan pane on the left (OpenSeadragon or Leaflet CRS.Simple over IIIF Level-0 or DZI tiles), Mapbox map on the right, point pairs, a residual per GCP (leave-one-out), switchable transform types, and an opacity/swipe preview. Reusable parts:
- @allmaps/transform (MIT): straight, helmert, polynomial 1-3, thinPlateSpline and projective, in both directions.
- Allmaps iiif-tiler (browser) or vips dzsave --layout iiif3 to make Level-0 tiles.
- @allmaps/io: generates GDAL scripts from Georeference Annotations.
- @allmaps/maplibre WarpedMapLayer: MapLibre only, no pitch; Mapbox GL is untested.
- MapWarper (Rails, MIT) as a UX reference.
- Leaflet.DistortableImage: 4-corner CSS only.

Quick preview in the browser: Mapbox GL JS image source with 4 corners is perspective-correct since v2.7.0 (verified in the CHANGELOG), so it is an exact homography preview. For a TPS preview, transform a mesh with @allmaps/transform and draw it in a Mapbox custom layer, or inverse-map a 2-4k px preview into a canvas/image source. gdal3.js (WASM) is a heavier option.

Downloading existing scans is free; on-demand scanning costs $30 per frame at 7 or 14 µm. A $5 order fee and 3-4 week turnaround appear in a USGS FAQ (seen only via a search snippet). Once scanned, frames become free to everyone in EarthExplorer.

Declass-3 (KH-9 panoramic) holdings at EROS are 'primarily over the United States, Antarctica, and the Arctic Circle'. However, the existing site's KH-9 high-resolution layers for 1976/1977/1980 credited to USGS suggest Bucharest frames exist.

For a ~24 km city crop, a 4-GCP projective warp of KH-4A/B is expected to give about 5-20 m near the scan centre but about 50-150+ m about 30° off-nadir. Dense GCPs with TPS or a 2nd-3rd order polynomial give about 1-3 px (about 3-10 m).
claims.source: Inference from panoramic geometry (ground position = H·tanθ, H about 150-185 km) plus literature figures above

claims.claim: SIFT/SURF-type matching is unstable on Corona. SuperGlue against 3 m PlanetScope with coarse-to-fine tiling worked in CoSP. The DLR 2026 benchmark shows pre-rectification greatly improves deep-matcher success: under 14% of raw images reach pixel accuracy, versus up to 30% after approximate orthorectification.

AROSICS local mode builds a dense tie-point grid (window 256 px, max_shift 5 px by default, RANSAC filter level 3) and exposes the tie points. It needs inputs that are already roughly geocoded and orthorectified, so it fits only as a final refinement step.

GDAL 3.11 added a homography transformer. gdalwarp uses it automatically for 4-5 GCPs, or it can be forced with -to SRC_METHOD=GCP_HOMOGRAPHY. More than 6 GCPs default to a 2nd-order polynomial. -tps needs at least N²·8 bytes of RAM. -refine_gcps works only with polynomial.

The latest GDAL is 3.13.3 (Aug 2026), and the official image ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-3.13.3 exists. The new 'gdal raster reproject' CLI (since 3.11) is the equivalent of gdalwarp and is multithreaded by default since 3.12.

Mapbox accepts only 8-bit GeoTIFFs, up to 10 GB via the Uploads API but 300 MB and 20 uploads per month via the Studio/Console. For large files it recommends EPSG:3857, 256x256 blocks, LZW, and removing alpha if applicable. Support for single-band grayscale is not documented.
The public-repo ubuntu-latest runner has 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM and a 14 GB SSD, is free and unlimited, and each job is capped at 6 h.

The Mapbox Satellite tile terms (2021 copy) forbid deriving or extracting data, including via tracing, from tiles including satellite imagery for any purpose. Esri World Imagery falls under the Esri Master License Agreement. Copernicus VHR mosaics are view-only WMS. ANCPI orthophoto WMS is restricted. Using these as an automatic GCP reference therefore carries license risk.
Sentinel-2 L2A COGs are openly available without auth on AWS Earth Search (collection sentinel-2-c1-l2a), alongside cop-dem-glo-30, and can be read with /vsicurl.
LightGlue code and weights are Apache-2.0; DISK is Apache-2.0 and ALIKED is BSD-3; SuperPoint is under a restrictive license. RoMa is listed as MIT on mirrors (upstream not verified).

Mapbox GL JS has drawn non-rectangular image/canvas/video sources with perspective correction since v2.7.0 (PR #11292), so a 4-corner image source is an exact homography preview. The current site uses v2.6.1, which predates this.

@allmaps/transform (MIT) supports straight, helmert, polynomial1-3, thinPlateSpline and projective with GcpTransformer in both directions. @allmaps/maplibre's WarpedMapLayer is a MapLibre CustomLayerInterface (no pitch, built for MapLibre 5), and Mapbox GL compatibility is undocumented. The Allmaps Editor needs IIIF images; Allmaps iiif-tiler makes Level-0 tiles in the browser.
Since Oct 2024, Cloud Storage for Firebase (including default buckets) requires the Blaze plan, so preview images and tiles cannot live in Firebase Storage on a Spark plan.
USGS M2M API password login was scheduled for deprecation on 2025-02-26 in favour of 'login-token' with an application token.
A prior academic study rectified a 1964 Corona of Bucharest by rubber sheeting (no RMSE given) and noted about 30 m of elevation difference in the area.

research.concrete_details:
ACQUISITION
- EarthExplorer → Declassified Data → Declass 1 (KH-4A/4B), Declass 2 (KH-7, KH-9 mapping camera), Declass 3 (KH-9 panoramic).
- Filter on "Download Available". Order unscanned frames at 7 µm ($30 per frame; FAQ snippet also says +$5 order fee).
- M2M API (application token, 'login-token'). Dataset names seen in clients: corona2, declassii. Declass 3 name not confirmed; use usgsxplore 'info' to list.
- Entity ID format (Declass-3): DDSMMMM-BOOOOOCFFF, with C = A/F/T camera. Corona example: DS1105-2248DF076 (F = forward, A = aft).
- Search EarthExplorer around Bucharest for the dates the old site used: 1966 KH-4A; 1976, 1977 and 1980 KH-9 panoramic; 1978 KH-9 mapping camera.

APPROXIMATE PIXEL SIZE AT 7 µm (inference: pixel size x altitude / focal length)
- KH-4B: about 1.7 m (f = 0.6096 m, about 150 km)
- KH-4A: about 2.1 m
- KH-9 panoramic: about 0.7-0.8 m (f = 1.524 m)
- KH-9 mapping camera: about 3.9 m sampling (6-9 m resolution)
- KH-7: 0.6-1.2 m resolution

BUCHAREST BBOX
- Lon 25.95-26.25, lat 44.33-44.54, about 23.8 x 23.3 km.
- In EPSG:3857: -te 2888740 5516653 2922137 5549392.

OUTPUT RESOLUTION (EPSG:3857 -tr; ground ≈ tr x cos 44.43°)
| Zoom | -tr | Ground pixel | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| z14 | 9.554629 | 6.8 m | KH-9 mapping camera |
| z15 | 4.777314 | 3.4 m | KH-9 mapping camera (finer option); 14 µm Corona |
| z16 | 2.388657 | 1.71 m | KH-4A/4B at 7 µm |
| z17 | 1.194329 | 0.85 m | KH-9 panoramic / KH-7 |

City size per zoom:
- z16: about 13,981 x 13,706 px ≈ 192 Mpx.
- z17: about 767 Mpx (RGB raw about 2.3 GB, under the 10 GB Mapbox limit).
- z18: about 3 Gpx (RGB raw about 9.2 GB). Avoid, or split into several tilesets.

PIPELINE (GitHub Actions, container ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-3.13.3 plus Python with OpenCV/torch-cpu/kornia/lightglue/arosics)
0) Download only the parts you need, never storing the archive:
   curl -sSL "$EE_URL" | tar -xzf - --wildcards '*_b.tif' '*_c.tif'
   Or read in place: gdalinfo /vsitar/scene.tgz/DS..._c.tif
1) Locate the city:
   - Fit a homography from the 4 metadata corners to the image corners and predict Bucharest's pixel position. Add a ±15-20 km margin, or more if a coarse match fails.
   - Better (inference): match the small EarthExplorer browse JPEG against Sentinel-2 first, then choose which segments to fetch.
2) Crop early, without resampling:
   gdal_translate -srcwin X0 Y0 W H -co TILED=YES -co COMPRESS=DEFLATE -co PREDICTOR=2 DS..._c.tif crop_c.tif
   Rotate aft-camera frames 180° for the matcher (OpenCV), and keep track of the rotation for GCP pixel coordinates.
3) If the city straddles parts, prefer georeferencing each segment independently: warp each into the same output (gdalwarp in1.vrt in2.vrt out.tif; the later input wins in the overlap) or use gdalbuildvrt. Otherwise stitch:
   image_mosaic DS_d.tif DS_c.tif DS_b.tif DS_a.tif -o full.tif --ot byte --overlap-width 7000 --blend-radius 2000 [--rotate] [--use-affine-transform]
   Or spymicmac join_hexagon (overlap search 2000 px, optional blend).
4) Radiometry:
   - Matching copy only: CLAHE in OpenCV.
   - Product: gdalinfo -stats -hist, then gdal_translate -ot Byte -scale P1 P99 1 255 (keep 0 as nodata).
5) Automatic GCPs:
   a) Coarse: downsample the crop to about 10 m. Reference is Sentinel-2 L2A from Earth Search (sentinel-2-c1-l2a), a summer scene with low clouds, B04 or visual band, read via /vsicurl/ with gdal_translate -projwin. Match with RoMa/LoFTR, or ALIKED/DISK+LightGlue, and fit a RANSAC homography.
   b) Pre-warp the crop into the reference grid with that homography.
   c) Fine: tile-wise matching (1024² tiles, 128-256 px overlap), or AROSICS COREG_LOCAL(grid_res≈64-128, window_size=(256,256), max_shift=5) on the pre-warped image against the highest-resolution reference you are licensed to use.
   d) Map the points back to original crop pixels with the inverse homography.
   e) Clean the points: RANSAC against a 2nd/3rd-order polynomial (residual threshold of about 2-3 px of reference GSD); spatial thinning to 1 point per 300-500 m cell; leave-one-out TPS residuals. Optionally smooth with scipy RBFInterpolator(smoothing>0) and resample to a 20x20-30x30 synthetic GCP grid so TPS cannot form outlier 'bubbles'.
   f) Hold out 10-20% of points as checkpoints and report checkpoint RMSE (not GCP RMSE).
6) Attach the GCPs (or use the Python gdal.Translate(GCPs=[gdal.GCP(lon,lat,0,px,ln)...]) for many points):
   gdal_translate -of VRT -a_srs EPSG:4326 -gcp <px> <line> <lon> <lat> ... crop_c.tif crop_c_gcps.vrt
7) Warp:
   gdalwarp -overwrite -t_srs EPSG:3857 -tps -r lanczos -te 2888740 5516653 2922137 5549392 -tr 2.388657 2.388657 -tap -srcnodata 0 -dstalpha -multi -wo NUM_THREADS=ALL_CPUS -wm 2G -et 0.05 -co TILED=YES -co BLOCKXSIZE=256 -co BLOCKYSIZE=256 -co COMPRESS=DEFLATE -co BIGTIFF=IF_SAFER crop_c_gcps.vrt warped.tif
   - Alternatives: -order 2|3 [-refine_gcps <tol_m> <min_gcps>]; homography with -to SRC_METHOD=GCP_HOMOGRAPHY (GDAL ≥3.11).
   - New CLI equivalent: gdal raster reproject.
   - Mask scan borders with -cutline or crop rather than relying only on nodata 0.
8) Mapbox upload GeoTIFF (8-bit). Grayscale-to-RGB is the safe choice; whether Mapbox accepts single-band uploads is unverified:
   gdal_translate -b 1 -b 1 -b 1 -b 2 -colorinterp red,green,blue,alpha -co TILED=YES -co BLOCKXSIZE=256 -co BLOCKYSIZE=256 -co COMPRESS=LZW warped.tif upload.tif
   If the bbox lies fully inside the valid footprint, use -b 1 -b 1 -b 1 and drop alpha (Mapbox suggests removing alpha). Upload through the Uploads API (10 GB limit), not Studio (300 MB).
9) Archive/preview COG:
   gdal_translate -of COG -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co QUALITY=85 -co BLOCKSIZE=256 -co OVERVIEW_RESAMPLING=AVERAGE warped.tif out.cog.tif
   With JPEG compression, alpha becomes a 1-bit mask. Alternatively -of COG -co TILING_SCHEME=GoogleMapsCompatible -co ZOOM_LEVEL=16 (the driver reprojects; ADD_ALPHA defaults to YES).
   Also export a downsampled preview (2-4k px JPEG/WebP) plus IIIF Level-0 tiles of the unwarped crop (vips dzsave crop.tif out --layout iiif3 --suffix .jpg) for the admin UI.

RESOURCE ESTIMATES (inference)
- KH-4A/B at 7 µm: download about 1.3 GB, crop 0.15-0.3 GB, warped 0.2-0.8 GB. Peak disk 3-4 GB if the archive is streamed. RAM 2-4 GB for GDAL with -wm 2G. TPS with ≤2,000 GCPs needs ≤32 MB of matrix memory. Time: download (variable) + matching on CPU about 5-30 min (LightGlue/LoFTR; RoMa slower) + warp/COG under 10 min. Fits comfortably in 6 h.
- KH-9 panoramic/KH-7 at 7 µm: multiple files of 0.7-1 GB each. Stream-extract only the members you need; jlumbroso/free-disk-space frees up to about 31 GB if needed. GDAL /vsitar/ reads .tgz in place; /vsicurl needs HTTP range support, and for tgz the read is sequential anyway.

BROWSER UX
- Left pane: OpenSeadragon or Leaflet CRS.Simple on IIIF/DZI tiles of the raw crop.
- Right pane: Mapbox GL JS v3 (current 3.32.0) with a satellite basemap plus an opacity/swipe overlay.
- GCP table with leave-one-out residuals (blue/yellow/red like MapWarper). Automatic GCPs are pre-loaded and coloured by confidence. A transform selector (projective / poly1-3 / TPS) uses @allmaps/transform. Once 4 or more GCPs exist, the cursor position is predicted in the other pane.
- Save GCPs to Firestore, then trigger the Action with workflow_dispatch or repository_dispatch.
- Preview options:
  (a) 4 GCPs: map.addSource('preview',{type:'image',url:previewJpg,coordinates:[TL,TR,BR,BL]}), perspective-correct since GL JS v2.7.0.
  (b) TPS: a Mapbox custom layer drawing a 64x64 mesh. Mesh vertices go through GcpTransformer(gcps,'thinPlateSpline').transformToGeo and then mapboxgl.MercatorCoordinate.fromLngLat. The texture is the preview JPEG.
  (c) Inverse-map in a Worker: evaluate the inverse TPS on a coarse grid with bilinear interpolation (like GDAL -et), write the result into a canvas, and display it as an axis-aligned image source.
  (d) gdal3.js 2.8.1 (WASM) running gdalwarp -tps on the 2k preview.
research.risks_and_unknowns:
- Coverage and availability: Declass-3 (KH-9 panoramic) at EROS is "primarily" US/Antarctic/Arctic. The old site's 1976-80 layers suggest Bucharest frames exist, but whether they are already scanned or need ordering must be checked in EarthExplorer. KH-7 coverage of Bucharest is unknown.
- On-demand scan details: the $5 order fee and 3-4 week turnaround come from an undated FAQ snippet. Orders appear to be UI-only, not M2M. Paid scans become public.
- I could not confirm the M2M dataset name for Declass-3 or the exact current download-request flow.
- Reference imagery licensing is the biggest non-technical risk. Mapbox tile terms (2021 copy) prohibit deriving or extracting data from satellite tiles. Esri World Imagery, the Copernicus VHR mosaic and the ANCPI WMS have restrictive or unclear terms. Sentinel-2 (open) is only 10 m, so fully automatic GCPs from open data alone may reach only about 5-15 m. Sub-pixel accuracy at 2 m or 0.8 m likely needs manual GCPs or a licensed reference. Whether a human placing GCPs while looking at Mapbox Satellite counts as 'tracing' is a legal question to raise with Mapbox; not legal advice.
- Matching robustness across 50-60 years of urban change (Civic Centre demolition, new estates, seasonal and shadow differences, film grain and scratches) is unproven for Bucharest. The literature shows learned matchers work with coarse-to-fine tiling and pre-rectification, yet benchmarks still report low pixel-accurate success rates. Plan for human QA.
- Scan geometry: part order and orientation vary (ASP reverses d→a; spymicmac says 'a' is left; aft frames need 180° rotation). Film deformation of up to about 6 px exists. KH-4/4A lack the PG stripes needed for bending correction.
- Panoramic distortion: with only a few GCPs, error depends heavily on where Bucharest falls in the scan. Prefer frames where the city is near the scan centre.
- TPS honours outliers exactly; GDAL TPS appears to offer no smoothing parameter (unverified). Needs robust filtering, and accuracy must be measured on checkpoints.
- Mapbox specifics are not fully documented: single-band grayscale support, alpha vs nodata transparency, and how max zoom is derived. Test with a small upload first. Studio uploads are limited to 300 MB and 20 per month, so use the Uploads API.
- Ubuntu apt GDAL is likely older than 3.11 (my assumption; unverified), so use the OSGeo container. gdal3.js is migrating to cpp.js, so its API may change.
- Allmaps WarpedMapLayer targets MapLibre and its Mapbox GL compatibility is untested. The Allmaps Editor requires IIIF hosting.
- Firebase Storage needs Blaze, so preview images and tiles must be hosted elsewhere: GitHub Pages or Releases, or a public repo branch (size limits apply).
- Accuracy figures for 4-GCP warps per camera are my own geometric inferences, not published benchmarks.
research.recommendation:
1. Treat USGS corners only as a search hint. Build a two-stage, segment-local pipeline in GitHub Actions on the OSGeo GDAL 3.13 container:
   - Stream-download only the needed scan parts.
   - Crop the Bucharest window with -srcwin.
   - Georeference each segment independently instead of stitching the whole frame; use ASP image_mosaic only if a city must span a seam and per-segment warps show visible seams.
   - Coarse GCPs: Sentinel-2 10 m (open) with a robust learned matcher (ALIKED/DISK+LightGlue or RoMa/LoFTR; avoid SuperPoint/SuperGlue weights for licensing reasons), then a RANSAC homography.
   - Fine GCPs: pre-warp, then tile matching or AROSICS local co-registration.
   - Filter outliers aggressively, optionally regularize to a synthetic GCP grid, then gdalwarp -tps -r lanczos to EPSG:3857 on a zoom-aligned bbox (z16 for KH-4A/B, z17 for KH-9 panoramic/KH-7, z14-15 for KH-9 mapping camera).
   - Output an 8-bit RGB(+alpha) GeoTIFF for the Mapbox Uploads API, plus a JPEG COG and a downsampled preview.
2. Always end with the admin reviewing in the browser. Use a MapWarper-style split view built on @allmaps/transform, Mapbox GL JS v3 image-source previews (homography) or a custom-layer mesh (TPS), and IIIF Level-0 tiles of the raw crop hosted on GitHub. Save GCPs to Firestore and re-run the Action. Report checkpoint RMSE, never GCP RMSE.
3. When buying from USGS:
   - First check "Download Available" (free) for the frames matching the old site's years: 1966 KH-4A; 1976/1977/1980 KH-9 panoramic; 1978 KH-9 mapping camera.
   - Order missing frames at 7 µm ($30 per frame).
   - Prefer frames where Bucharest lies near the scan centre and with low cloud and snow.
   - Confirm the licensing of any high-resolution reference used for automatic GCPs before relying on Mapbox or Esri imagery for anything beyond human visual comparison.

The 100 m figure is in Sec. 2.1 ('errors of 100m or more on flat terrain', about Casana 2003). The 2OC abstract (via search) gives orientation SD under 2 px and checkpoint SD better than 4 m. 2OC used Google Earth orthophotos as its reference, which is a licence issue if copied. The mdpi page returned 403.

verified.claim: For a ~24 km crop, a 4-GCP projective warp gives about 5-20 m near the scan centre and 50-150+ m at ~30° off-nadir; dense GCPs with TPS or polynomial give about 1-3 px.
verified.correction: This is the researcher's own geometric derivation and is plausible, but no primary source reports these numbers for a city crop. A search summary (not opened) mentions affine fits of about 10-20 m with dense GCPs versus about 130 m with widely spread GCPs on Corona, and a West Siberia study reporting 2.7-3.1 m RMSE with 3rd-order polynomial and 40+ GCPs. Treat these as targets and measure on held-out checkpoints.
verified.source: Inference; search results pointing to https://intarch.ac.uk/journal/issue32/2/2.1.html and b2find West Siberia dataset

verified.claim: SIFT/SURF are unstable on Corona (2OC); SuperGlue against 3 m PlanetScope with coarse-to-fine tiling worked in CoSP; in the DLR 2026 benchmark under 14% of raw images reach pixel accuracy versus up to 30% after approximate orthorectification.
verified.correction: Confirmed: CoSP used SuperGlue against a 3 m PlanetScope mosaic and 15 m Landsat-7 pan, with 1920x1440 patches, and was weak in forest. Confirmed: DLR figures (<14% raw; up to 30% with JamMa, SIFT and SuperPoint+LightGlue after approximate ortho; ELoFTR and RoMa more robust on raw images). But the DLR images are 51 modern aerial photos, not historical satellite film, so applying the result to Corona is an inference. Not verified: the claim that 2OC says SIFT/SURF are unstable (abstract not reachable; snippets only mention weak texture and strong distortion).

verified.claim: GDAL 3.11 added a homography transformer; gdalwarp uses it automatically for 4-5 GCPs or via -to SRC_METHOD=GCP_HOMOGRAPHY; more than 6 GCPs default to 2nd-order polynomial; -tps needs at least N²·8 bytes; -refine_gcps works only with polynomial.
verified.correction: NEWS.md 3.11.0 lists 'New Transform type: Homography (#11940)'. alg/gdaltransformer.cpp picks homography when SRC_METHOD is unset and the GCP count is 4 or 5. Corrections: (a) 3.12.3 fixed a 'bad scaling factor on overviews (3.11.0 regression)' in the homography transformer, so require GDAL ≥3.12.3, not ≥3.11. (b) In gdal_crs.cpp the automatic order is 2 for 6 or more GCPs, so 6 GCPs give an exact 2nd-order fit with zero residuals. Always pass -order or SRC_METHOD explicitly. (c) From reading gdalwarp_lib.cpp, -order only sets MAX_GCP_ORDER, so with 4-5 GCPs it probably does not override homography; use -to SRC_METHOD=GCP_POLYNOMIAL (inference). (d) The gdalwarp HTML docs do not mention GCP_HOMOGRAPHY; it is documented only in source and NEWS. TPS RAM and refine_gcps statements confirmed from the gdalwarp docs.

verified.claim: Mapbox accepts only 8-bit GeoTIFF: 10 GB via the Uploads API, 300 MB and 20 uploads per month in Studio; recommends EPSG:3857, 256x256 blocks, LZW, no alpha; single-band support undocumented.
verified.correction: The numbers are right, but the routing advice is outdated. (1) The Uploads API page now carries a legacy note: 'We recommend you use the Mapbox Tiling Service (MTS) to create tilesets instead of the Uploads API'. The troubleshooting page sends files over 300 MB to MTS. (2) Raster MTS docs say it 'can process panchromatic, 3-band RGB, or 4-band RGBA GeoTIFF' into webp/png/jpg tiles, so single-band IS documented for MTS. Use MTS with a 1-band upload rather than duplicating gray into RGB. (3) The Uploads API cannot set maxzoom; MTS recipes can (the example uses minzoom 16, maxzoom 18).

verified.claim: Public-repo ubuntu-latest runners have 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD, are free and unlimited, and jobs are capped at 6 h.
verified.correction: Confirmed; ubuntu-latest maps to 24.04. Also relevant: workflow runs are capped at 35 days; artifact storage is only 500 MB on the Free plan and cache is 10 GB per repo, so multi-GB intermediates cannot be passed between jobs as artifacts. Keep the pipeline in one job or use external storage.

verified.claim: Mapbox tile terms (2021 copy) forbid deriving data from tiles 'for any purpose' and the OSM exception exists only in a third-party post; Esri World Imagery is under the Esri MLA; Copernicus VHR is view-only WMS; ANCPI WMS is restricted.
verified.correction: The cited 'Mapbox tiles 06-2021' page is a reseller (Precisely) licence, not Mapbox's own terms. Mapbox's own Product Terms (PDF dated July 21, 2026) say: §1.6 no tracing, deriving or extracting, EXCEPT tracing satellite-only maps into derivative vector datasets for non-commercial purposes or for OpenStreetMap (so the OSM exception is official). §1.9 bans bulk or automated queries and downloading or caching. §2.8.2 says 'Customer shall not use Mapbox's satellite and/or aerial imagery to improve the accuracy of or otherwise enhance any imagery'. That clause makes even MANUAL GCP picking against Mapbox Satellite a likely violation, not just automatic matching (legal reading is my inference). Esri, as quoted on the OSM wiki, grants tracing 'in the creation of vector data' only; georeferencing is not addressed. Copernicus VHR 2021 is WMS-only 'due to license restrictions'. VHR 2024 is limited to authorised user categories. ANCPI orthophoto view service has limited public access under INSPIRE Art. 13(1)(e) with tariffs (record from 2021).

1. LICENSING BLOCKS THE PROPOSED ADMIN UX: Mapbox Product Terms (PDF dated July 21, 2026) §2.8.2 forbid using Mapbox satellite or aerial imagery 'to improve the accuracy of or otherwise enhance any imagery'. §1.9 bans automated or bulk queries and downloading. The planned right-hand pane (Mapbox satellite basemap used to pick GCPs) and any automatic matching against Mapbox Satellite are therefore likely non-compliant (legal reading is my inference; ask Mapbox to confirm). The 2OC paper used Google Earth as its reference, which also cannot be copied. Mapbox Satellite may still be shown to end users as a basemap.
2. MAPBOX PUBLISHING PATH CHANGED: the Uploads API is marked legacy and MTS is recommended. Raster MTS accepts panchromatic (1-band) GeoTIFF and lets the recipe set min/maxzoom; the Uploads API cannot set maxzoom. Pricing is now per MB plus compute units (CUs) (legacy km² pricing applies only to pre-2024-08-01 accounts). Free tier per month: 10,000 MB and 20 CUs of processing; 750 hosting days and 25 average hosted tilesets. Raster CUs scale with resolution, bands and extent, so repeated z17-18 city re-publishes could exceed 20 CUs. Measure with `tilesets estimate-cu` or one test job. Uploading gray as RGB triples the MB billed.
3. GDAL: pin ≥3.12.3, because of the homography overview-scaling regression from 3.11.0. With 6 GCPs the automatic polynomial order is 2, an exact fit with zero residuals. With 4-5 GCPs, -order probably does not override homography. Always set SRC_METHOD or -order explicitly.
4. USGS ACCESS: M2M needs a separate access approval (24-48 business hours) in addition to an ERS account and an application token. Paid scan orders are placed in the EarthExplorer cart by credit card, take 3-4 weeks and are non-refundable, so ordering cannot be automated from the admin page or Actions. The old site's 1966/1976/1977/1978/1980 frames were evidently scanned already and are probably free downloads now, so 'buying' may cost $0 except for unscanned frames.
5. NO BLAZE MEANS NO SERVER SIDE: Firebase Storage has been unusable on Spark since Feb 3, 2026, and Cloud Functions also need Blaze. Previews and IIIF tiles must live elsewhere, e.g. the GitHub repo or Pages, GitHub Releases, or Mapbox. GitHub Pages size limits were not verified. Triggering Actions from a static admin page needs a token with Actions write permission held in the browser (workflow_dispatch). The alternative is a scheduled Actions job polling Firestore, but public-repo schedules are auto-disabled after 60 days without repository activity.
6. ACTIONS STORAGE: free-plan artifact storage is 500 MB and cache is 10 GB per repo, so download, crop, warp and upload must run in a single job. Logs of a public repo are public, so never echo signed USGS URLs or tokens.
7. The DLR benchmark used modern aerial imagery, so its success rates do not transfer directly to 1960s film. Plan for a manual GCP fallback as the norm, not the exception.
8. Preview and output mismatch: @allmaps fits transforms in Web Mercator, while GDAL fits GCPs in their own SRS (EPSG:4326), and allmaps' backward transform is not the exact inverse. The browser TPS preview can therefore differ slightly from the gdalwarp output (inference). Allmaps packages are still 1.0.0-beta, there is no Mapbox adapter, and gdal3.js is LGPL.

research.area: Mapbox (2026) for publishing and displaying historical raster layers: GL JS v3, Uploads API vs MTS, pricing, tileset privacy, tokens, and self-hosted alternatives (PMTiles/XYZ on GitHub Pages, Releases, R2)
research.summary:
This covers your request to use our own USGS-purchased imagery (not fostulbucuresti). That imagery is US-government public domain, so making the tilesets public raises no licensing problem (my inference).

1) GL JS version. The latest stable Mapbox GL JS is v3.32.0, published 2026-09-29. v3.33.0-rc.1 (2026-10-06) is a pre-release whose breaking changes are about the RTL text plugin, which does not matter for Romanian. The docs CDN snippets use https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v3.32.0/mapbox-gl.js and .css. v3 requires WebGL2.
Features useful here:
- Standard style slots: 'bottom' sits above polygons. 'middle' sits above roads and below 3D buildings and labels, which is where to put historical imagery so labels stay readable. 'top' sits above POI labels and below place/transit labels. Slots can be read or changed with getSlot/setSlot (3.3.0).
- Raster paint properties: raster-opacity, raster-color (3.0), raster-emissive-strength (3.1), and raster-allow-draping (3.29, no longer experimental since 3.31).
- Image source: a georeferenced image placed by 4 corners. Good for a quick admin preview before tiling.
- Globe projection is the default on low-zoom v3 maps.
- Swipe compare: the docs example uses mapbox-gl-compare v0.4.0. npm latest is 0.6.0 (2026-06-22), and I confirmed api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/plugins/mapbox-gl-compare/v0.6.0/mapbox-gl-compare.js exists. Options are orientation (vertical/horizontal) and mousemove. Methods: setSlider, the 'slideend' event, remove.

2) Uploads API. It is still documented but marked "Note (legacy): Use the Mapbox Tiling Service". No end-of-life date is given. The flow you described is correct:
- POST /uploads/v1/{username}/credentials (uploads:write) returns accessKeyId, bucket, key, secretAccessKey, sessionToken and url. The bucket is in us-east-1.
- PUT the file to S3 with those temporary credentials.
- POST /uploads/v1/{username} with {tileset:'ventura86.x', url, name} (uploads:write).
- Poll GET /uploads/v1/{username}/{upload_id} (uploads:read) until complete=true; progress goes 0 to 1.
Limits and behaviour:
- GeoTIFF limit is 10 GB, and only 8-bit GeoTIFFs are accepted.
- Mapbox recommends EPSG:3857, 256x256 blocks, LZW compression and no alpha band.
- Max and min zoom are picked automatically from pixel resolution; you cannot set them.
- Re-posting the same tileset id replaces the data, but only for tilesets that were created by the Uploads API.
- The rate limit is 60 requests per minute.

MTS raster is the recommended path. You create a tileset source, create a tileset with a recipe of type 'raster' (version 1, explicit minzoom/maxzoom, bands chosen with colorinterp filters), publish, and poll the job. This uses tilesets:write and tilesets:read. Limits:
- Input must be uint8 GeoTIFF or COG, panchromatic, RGB or RGBA, not YCbCr.
- Each file can be up to 20 GB, with up to 10 files and 50 GB per source.
- Output is webp/png/jpg tiles, added in GL JS as type 'raster' with url 'mapbox://user.tileset'.
- To update, replace the source (PUT) and re-publish. New tiles only appear as cached tiles expire.
- Delete with DELETE /tilesets/v1/{id}.
- Set privacy with PATCH /tilesets/v1/{id} {private:false}; tilesets are private by default.

Browser CORS: I probed this myself, it is not documented.
- api.mapbox.com answers preflights for /uploads/v1/.../credentials and /tilesets/v1/sources/... with access-control-allow-origin for any origin.
- The S3 bucket tilestream-tilesets-production answers PUT preflights with ACAO * and allows the authorization, x-amz-date, x-amz-content-sha256 and x-amz-security-token headers. That bucket name comes from historical Mapbox tooling; I did not confirm it is the bucket the current credentials endpoint returns.
- mapbox-sdk-js documents passing a Blob to createTilesetSource in the browser.
So browser uploads look technically possible, but every path needs a secret (sk) token in the browser.

3) Pricing as of 2026-10, from mapbox.com/pricing:
- Web map loads: up to 50,000 free per month, then $5.00 per 1,000 (50k–100k), $4.00 (100k–200k), $3.00 (200k–1M), $2.50 (1M–5M). A map load includes unlimited Vector Tiles API and Raster Tiles API requests.
- Raster Tiles API (direct /v4 use, e.g. from Leaflet): 750,000 free per month, then $0.25, $0.20, $0.15 per 1,000.
- Static Tiles API: 200,000 free, then $0.50, $0.40, $0.30 per 1,000.
- Tileset processing (new model for tilesets since 2024-08-01; older tilesets are on km²-based legacy pricing): 10,000 MB per month free, then $0.007/MB. 20 compute units (CUs) per month free, then $0.90/CU for 21–1,000.
- Tileset hosting is billed in "tileset hosting days" (one tileset hosted for one day), and file size does not matter. 750 per month are free, which is about 24–25 tilesets hosted all month. Then $0.01370 per day for 751–3,000 (about $0.41 per tileset per 30 days), $0.01096 for 3,001–30,000, and lower tiers after that.

Big 2026 caveat: an account with no payment method is on a trial.
- Trial limits: 5,000 web map loads per month, MTS processing of 1 GB and 10 CU, and only 75 hosting days.
- The Raster Tiles API is not accessible during the trial.
- You get one token and cannot create, rotate or delete tokens.
- So the ventura86 account almost certainly needs a card on file, which is the same blocker as Firebase Blaze.

Studio/Console uploads: the current Console docs say GeoTIFF uploads are limited to 300 MB each and 20 uploads per month and go through the Uploads API. The Studio manual page contradicts itself between versions: one copy says Studio uploads have no processing or hosting charges, another says they are billed. The Studio UI text you quoted suggests hosting days are billed.

4) Privacy and URL restrictions.
- Public tilesets can be used with any Mapbox user's token (they need the tileset ID but cannot edit it). Private tilesets only work with the owner's tokens.
- URL restrictions: up to 100 URLs per token. Only the domain is required. Subdomains and subpaths match, paths are case-sensitive, no wildcards or IPs. A Referer header is required, so no-referrer and same-origin policies break it. localhost must be listed explicitly. Needs GL JS 0.53.1 or later. You cannot add restrictions to the default public token.
- Browsers' default referrer policy (strict-origin-when-cross-origin) sends only the origin to api.mapbox.com. So restrict to 'https://ventura8.github.io' rather than the /bucurestiuldisparut.github.io path (my inference, consistent with the Mapbox Search JS guidance).

5) Tokens API.
- POST /tokens/v2/{username} needs tokens:write. Body: note, scopes, allowedUrls.
- Whether a token is pk or sk depends only on its scopes: any secret scope makes it sk. A token cannot have more scopes than the token that creates it. The secret value is shown only once. 100 requests per minute.
- Temporary tokens: expire within 1 hour at most, cannot be revoked, and cannot have URL restrictions.
- Secret scopes include uploads:read/list/write, tilesets:read/list/write, styles:write/list, tokens:read/write and others.
- For CI, use a dedicated sk token with only tilesets:write, tilesets:read and tilesets:list (MTS path), or uploads:write and uploads:read (Uploads path). No tokens:write, styles:write or user:write. Store it as a GitHub Actions secret.

6) Alternatives if Mapbox hosting gets too expensive.
- Mapbox GL JS has no addProtocol; that is a MapLibre API. Instead it has a TileProvider API (3.21.0) with an official PMTiles plugin (mapbox-gl-pmtiles-provider.js, loaded on demand). Raster and raster-dem PMTiles support came in 3.23.0, and a PMTiles transformRequest fix in 3.32.0.
- The official example uses a plain https URL ending in .pmtiles. Its only example is vector; raster PMTiles is supported per the changelog but I found no official raster example.
- Plain XYZ raster sources ('tiles':[...], tileSize, scheme xyz/tms, bounds, minzoom/maxzoom) work as normal.
- Important: GL JS v3 still bills a map load on every map initialisation, even when no Mapbox tiles are used.
- GitHub Pages: published site at most 1 GB, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10-minute deploy timeout. Git blocks files over 100 MiB. I verified Pages returns access-control-allow-origin:* and 206 range responses, so PMTiles on Pages works if the total fits in 1 GB.
- GitHub Release assets: each must be under 2 GiB, up to 1,000 assets per release, no total or bandwidth cap. But the downloads redirect to a storage host without CORS headers (third-party reports), so they cannot be read from the browser directly. Use Releases only as archive or CI storage.
- Cloudflare R2: 10 GB-month storage, 1M Class A and 10M Class B operations free per month, egress free. You must configure CORS (allow range and if-match, expose etag). Third-party guides say enabling R2 needs a payment method.
- GDAL's PMTiles driver (3.8+) is vector-only. To make raster PMTiles, use gdal_translate -of MBTiles plus gdaladdo, then 'pmtiles convert'.

GL JS
- Script and stylesheet:
  <script src="https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v3.32.0/mapbox-gl.js"></script>
  <link href="https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v3.32.0/mapbox-gl.css" rel="stylesheet">
