- Recommendation: keep mapbox-gl as an external, loaded from api.mapbox.com, rather than bundling it into the engine.
- Compare plugin: https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/plugins/mapbox-gl-compare/v0.6.0/mapbox-gl-compare.js and .css.
  new mapboxgl.Compare(beforeMap, afterMap, '#container', {orientation:'vertical'|'horizontal', mousemove:true}); compare.setSlider(x); compare.on('slideend', e => e.currentPosition); compare.remove().
- Historical layer under labels:
  map.addSource('corona1968', {type:'raster', url:'mapbox://ventura86.corona1968', tileSize:256});
  map.addLayer({id:'corona1968', type:'raster', source:'corona1968', slot:'middle', paint:{'raster-opacity':0.85, 'raster-emissive-strength':1, 'raster-fade-duration':0}});
- Other paint properties: raster-resampling ('linear'|'nearest'), raster-contrast, raster-brightness-min/max, raster-saturation, raster-color (3.0+), raster-allow-draping (3.29+). Use map.setPaintProperty(id, 'raster-opacity', v) for the opacity slider.
- Preview an untiled scan: {type:'image', url, coordinates:[[TL],[TR],[BR],[BL]]}.
- Non-Mapbox tiles: {type:'raster', tiles:['https://host/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp'], tileSize:256, minzoom, maxzoom, bounds:[w,s,e,n], scheme:'xyz'}.
- PMTiles (>=3.23 for raster): {type:'raster', url:'https://ventura8.github.io/.../corona1968.pmtiles'}. Inference: a plain .pmtiles URL triggers the on-demand plugin, per the vector example.

Uploads API (legacy), base https://api.mapbox.com/uploads/v1
1. POST /{username}/credentials?access_token=sk (uploads:write). Response: {accessKeyId, bucket, key, secretAccessKey, sessionToken, url}. S3 region us-east-1.
2. s3.putObject({Bucket:bucket, Key:key, Body:file}) using the temporary credentials.
3. POST /{username} with JSON {"tileset":"ventura86.corona1968", "url":<url from step 1>, "name":"Corona 1968"} (uploads:write).
   - Tileset id is at most 32 characters after the username; only '-' and '_' allowed. Name at most 64 characters.
   - Response: {complete, tileset, error, id, name, modified, created, owner, progress}.
4. GET /{username}/{upload_id} (uploads:read). Poll until complete==true or error is set.
- GET /{username}?limit=100&reverse (uploads:list).
- DELETE /{username}/{upload_id} removes only the status record.
- Limits: TIFF/GeoTIFF 10 GB, MBTiles 25 GB, 60 requests/min.

MTS raster, base https://api.mapbox.com/tilesets/v1
- POST /sources/{username}/{source_id} multipart file=@x.tif (tilesets:write). PUT on the same path replaces the source. CLI: tilesets upload-raster-source ventura86 corona1968-src x.tif [--replace].
- POST /{tileset_id} {"recipe":{...}, "name":"..."}. Recipe:
  {"version":1, "type":"raster", "sources":[{"uri":"mapbox://tileset-source/ventura86/corona1968-src"}], "minzoom":10, "maxzoom":17, "layers":{"RGB":{"source_rules":{"filter":[["==",["get","colorinterp"],"red"], ...]}}}}
  The single-band (panchromatic) filter value is undocumented; possibly "gray". Test it.
- POST /{tileset_id}/publish returns job_id. Poll GET /{tileset_id}/jobs/{job_id} (tilesets:read).
- PATCH /{tileset_id}/recipe updates the recipe. PATCH /{tileset_id} {"private":false, "name", "attribution"} sets privacy. DELETE /{tileset_id}.
- Limits: 20 GB per file, 10 files and 50 GB per source. Rate limits: create source 100/min, publish 2/min, reads 3,000/min.
- CLI: pip mapbox-tilesets 2.2.0 (Python >=3.10). Env var MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN.

Max zoom from resolution (my inference; standard Web Mercator maths, not a Mapbox-published formula)
- Ground resolution at zoom z for 256 px tiles = 156543.03 × cos(lat) / 2^z m/px. Bucharest is at lat 44.43°, cos ≈ 0.714.
- z15 ≈ 3.41 m, z16 ≈ 1.71 m, z17 ≈ 0.85 m, z18 ≈ 0.43 m.
- So Corona KH-4B (~1.8 m) → maxzoom 16; KH-9 (~0.6–1.2 m) → 17; KH-7 Gambit (~0.6 m or better) → 17–18. GL JS overzooms beyond maxzoom up to z22.

Pricing (mapbox.com/pricing, as of 2026-10)
- Map loads (web): ≤50k free, then $5.00/1k (to 100k), $4.00 (to 200k), $3.00 (to 1M), $2.50 (to 5M).
- Raster Tiles API: ≤750k free, then $0.25/1k (to 2M), $0.20 (to 4M), $0.15.
- Static Tiles API: ≤200k free, then $0.50/$0.40/$0.30.
- Vector Tiles API: ≤200k free, then $0.25/$0.20/$0.15.
- Processing: ≤10,000 MB free, then $0.007/MB. ≤20 CU free, then $0.90 (21–1,000), $0.85 (1,001–5,000), $0.80 (5,001–10,000).
- Hosting days: ≤750 free; $0.01370 (751–3,000); $0.01096 (3,001–30,000); $0.00822 (to 300k); $0.00548 (to 600k); $0.00274 (600k+).
- Worked examples:
  - 40 tilesets × 30 days = 1,200 days → 450 billable × $0.0137 ≈ $6.17/month.
  - 100 tilesets = 3,000 days → 2,250 billable ≈ $30.8/month.
- Trial account (no card): 5,000 map loads, 1 GB / 10 CU processing, 75 hosting days, no Raster Tiles API, one token, no token management.

Tokens
- POST https://api.mapbox.com/tokens/v2/ventura86?access_token=sk(with tokens:write) with body {"note":"bucuresti public", "scopes":["styles:read","styles:tiles","fonts:read","datasets:read"], "allowedUrls":["https://ventura8.github.io","http://localhost"]}.
  - Public scopes: styles:tiles, styles:read, fonts:read, datasets:read.
- Temporary token body: {"expires":"<ISO, ≤1h ahead>", "scopes":[...]}.
- List scopes: GET /scopes/v1/{username} (scopes:list).
- CI secret token MAPBOX_SK_CI:
  - MTS path: tilesets:write, tilesets:read, tilesets:list.
  - Uploads path: add uploads:write, uploads:read, uploads:list.
  - Add styles:read/styles:write only if CI edits styles.
  - Never tokens:write or user:write.
- Rotation: create new token → swap the GitHub secret → delete the old one. Revocation is immediate except for cached responses.

Self-hosting
- GitHub Pages: site ≤1 GB, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10 builds/hour (not for Actions deploys), 10-minute deploy timeout. Verified ACAO:* and Range→206.
- Git: per-file block >100 MiB (warning >50 MiB), browser uploads ≤25 MiB; repository ideally <1 GB.
- Releases: each asset <2 GiB, ≤1,000 per release, no total/bandwidth cap; no CORS on the redirected download host.
- R2: 10 GB-month, 1M Class A / 10M Class B free; $0.015/GB-month; $4.50 per million Class A, $0.36 per million Class B; egress free. CORS JSON: AllowedMethods GET/HEAD, AllowedHeaders range and if-match, ExposeHeaders etag.
- Raster PMTiles pipeline:
  gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:3857 → gdal_translate -of MBTiles -co TILE_FORMAT=WEBP (or JPEG) → gdaladdo -r average x.mbtiles 2 4 8 16 ... → pmtiles convert x.mbtiles x.pmtiles
research.risks_and_unknowns:
- Payment method on Mapbox (biggest risk). If ventura86 has no card, it is on trial limits: 5,000 map loads, 75 hosting days (≈2 tilesets), 1 GB / 10 CU processing, no Raster Tiles API, and no token creation or rotation. That blocks the whole Mapbox-hosted plan. Check the account status in the Mapbox Console. The docs give no trial duration and do not say whether older accounts are exempt.
- Raster CU consumption is undocumented. The docs say it varies with resolution, bands and extent and point to an 'estimate-cu' tool I could not find in tilesets-cli 2.2.0 (PyPI 2026-01-07). A multi-GB KH-9 or Gambit mosaic could use well over 20 free CUs. Do a small test upload and read the Statistics page.
- Studio/Console free-upload policy is contradictory: one Studio manual page says free with no hosting charges (20 per month, 300 MB), another says billed. Assume hosting days apply to every custom tileset.
- Single-band (panchromatic) recipes. Raster MTS claims panchromatic support, but every example is RGB colorinterp filters. Uploads API single-band handling is not documented either. Fallback: expand gray to 3-band RGB with gdal_translate -b 1 -b 1 -b 1 (triples size) or test the 'gray' filter.
- NoData and transparency. Studio-uploaded GeoTIFFs are served as JPEG, so NoData shows black. GL JS gets webp when the browser supports it. Collars of scanned frames need correct NoData=0, and true black film pixels must be shifted to 1.
- Raster PMTiles in GL JS. Only the vector example is official; raster support is stated in the 3.23.0 changelog. The plugin loads on demand from api.mapbox.com, so a strict CSP must allow it. The TileProvider API is new; check its maturity before relying on it.
- Browser-side uploads. CORS is permissive by my own probes, not by documentation, and the S3 bucket name I tested comes from historical tooling. Every browser path puts an sk token in the browser. Firebase without Blaze has no Cloud Functions to mint temporary tokens. Options: run uploads in GitHub Actions (admin page triggers workflow_dispatch), or use a small free Cloudflare Worker to verify the Firebase ID token and mint a 1-hour temporary token. The Worker option is my inference.
- URL restrictions are best-effort (Referer can be spoofed outside browsers). Path-based restriction likely fails because of the default strict-origin-when-cross-origin policy. Restricting to ventura8.github.io allows all of that user's Pages sites.
- Mapbox GL JS v3 bills a map load on every initialisation even with self-hosted tiles. Moving off Mapbox hosting saves hosting/processing costs, not map-load costs. Only switching to MapLibre avoids map loads.
- GitHub Pages: 1 GB cap and "not a free file host for business" terms; the 100 GB/month soft bandwidth could be hit by a popular site. GitHub Releases cannot serve PMTiles to browsers (no CORS). R2 likely needs a payment method on Cloudflare.
- Pricing tiers on mapbox.com can change; I read them on 2026-10-11. Tilesets created before 2024-08-01 may be on legacy km²-based pricing; the docs say to email tilesets-pricing@mapbox.com.
- Uploads API is legacy and could be retired without a published date. MTS tilesets cannot be replaced through the Uploads API.
research.recommendation:
1. Engine
- Pin GL JS v3.32.0 from api.mapbox.com and keep it external to the jsDelivr engine bundle. Treat 3.33 as a later upgrade.
- Basemap: Mapbox Standard (or Standard Satellite). Put historical layers in slot 'middle' with raster-opacity driven by a UI slider and raster-emissive-strength:1.
- Swipe: mapbox-gl-compare v0.6.0.
- Admin preview: an 'image' source for georeferenced but not yet tiled scans.

2. Publishing path
- Use MTS raster (Tilesets API v1), not the legacy Uploads API. It gives explicit minzoom/maxzoom (≈16 for Corona, 17–18 for KH-9/KH-7 over Bucharest), multi-file sources up to 50 GB, a documented replace-source and re-publish flow, and PATCH {private:false}.
- Run it from GitHub Actions: GDAL warp to EPSG:3857 uint8 COG with NoData 0 → tilesets upload-raster-source → create/publish → poll the job → write the tileset id and metadata to Firestore.
- Keep one tileset per historical epoch or mosaic (e.g. 'ventura86.corona-1968-buc'), not per frame, to stay within 750 free hosting days (~24 tilesets).
- Make tilesets public only if you want other accounts to reuse them; this is not required for your own pk token.
- Keep the Uploads API as a fallback; it is also CORS-capable, but legacy.

3. Tokens
- Public pk token: scopes styles:read, styles:tiles, fonts:read; allowedUrls https://ventura8.github.io plus http://localhost for development; no path, because of referrer behaviour.
- CI sk token: only tilesets:read, tilesets:write and tilesets:list, stored as a GitHub Actions secret.
- Do not put any sk token in the admin page. The admin page should trigger a workflow_dispatch instead. If browser-direct uploads are ever needed, mint 1-hour temporary tokens from a small Cloudflare Worker that verifies the Firebase ID token.

4. Before building
- Confirm the Mapbox account has a payment method; otherwise the trial limits make the plan unworkable.
- Run one test MTS raster job on a real KH-4B Bucharest crop to measure CUs and MB, since the free 20 CU/month may only cover a few large mosaics.

5. Fallback design
- Make the engine's layer config accept either 'mapbox://' tileset URLs or https .pmtiles/XYZ URLs, so heavy layers can move to PMTiles without code changes.
- Hosting: GitHub Pages (≤1 GB total, CORS and Range verified) or Cloudflare R2 (10 GB free, zero egress, CORS config needed, likely needs a card). Not GitHub Releases (no CORS).
- PMTiles via the GDAL MBTiles driver plus 'pmtiles convert'.
- Remember that GL JS map loads (50k/month free with a card) are billed regardless of where the tiles live.

verified.claim: 1. The latest stable Mapbox GL JS is v3.32.0 (published 2026-09-29), and v3.33.0-rc.1 (2026-10-06) is a pre-release whose breaking changes are only about the RTL text plugin.
verified.correction: The version and dates are correct. npm dist-tags show latest=3.32.0 (2026-09-29T13:53Z) and next=3.33.0-rc.1 (2026-10-06), and the GitHub release is marked prerelease=true. Small correction: 3.33.0-rc.1 has a second breaking change. The base size of icons inside text-field is now calculated at the tile zoom with the largest text size, so icons can render smaller. It also removes setRTLTextPlugin, getRTLTextPluginStatus and PluginStatus outright. Neither change matters for a Romanian raster map. 3.33.0 GA will probably ship within days, so pin an exact version.

verified.claim: 2. The CDN URLs are https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v3.32.0/mapbox-gl.js and .css. The compare plugin v0.6.0 is on api.mapbox.com, and jsDelivr mirrors mapbox-gl@3.32.0.
verified.correction: All of these returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-11: v3.32.0 .js and .css, mapbox-gl-compare v0.6.0 and v0.4.0, and cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mapbox-gl@3.32.0/dist/mapbox-gl.js. The current docs examples already reference v3.32.0. mapbox-gl-compare 0.6.0 was published on npm 2026-06-22, while the docs example still uses v0.4.0.

verified.claim: 3. Standard style slots: 'bottom' is above polygons, 'middle' is above roads and behind 3D buildings, 'top' is above POI labels and behind place/transit labels. Layers use a 'slot' property.
verified.correction: The slot descriptions match the docs. The docs also note that 'top' is designed for symbol layers. The researcher missed a caveat on the same page: on globe or terrain, draped layers (raster, fill, line, hillshade) are batched and rendered under all symbols, whatever slot they are in. 'middle' also sits behind 3D buildings, so modern Standard 3D buildings and landmarks will draw on top of 1960s imagery unless they are turned off through the Standard style config (my inference). The slot property needs GL JS ≥3.0.0. getSlot/setSlot came in 3.3.0 and getSlots in 3.5.0.

verified.claim: (Summary) raster-allow-draping was added in 3.29 and has not been experimental since 3.31.
verified.correction: The 3.31.0 changelog does say 'Remove the experimental flag from raster-allow-draping'. However, the property is missing from the published 3.31.0, 3.32.0 and 3.33.0-rc.1 builds: grep finds 0 occurrences in both dist/style-spec and dist/mapbox-gl.js. It is present in 3.29.0 and 3.30.0, where the spec lists sdk-support js 3.28.0 and experimental:true. It is also absent from the main-branch v8.json and from the docs style-spec page. Do not rely on it.

verified.claim: (Summary) Globe projection is the default on low-zoom v3 maps.
verified.correction: This is imprecise. Globe is the default in the latest Mapbox styles (Standard and v12). Maps whose style sets no projection default to Mercator. It is not a GL JS v3 engine default.

verified.claim: 4. The Uploads API is marked legacy, Mapbox recommends MTS instead, and no end-of-life date is published.
verified.correction: The page has the banner 'Note (legacy): Use the Mapbox Tiling Service'. No end-of-life date is given.

verified.claim: 5. Uploads flow: POST /uploads/v1/{username}/credentials (uploads:write), then S3 PUT in us-east-1, then POST /uploads/v1/{username} {tileset,url,name}, then GET status (uploads:read). Listing needs uploads:list. Rate limit is 60 requests/min.
verified.correction: Every step matches the docs. The response fields are accessKeyId, bucket, key, secretAccessKey, sessionToken and url, and the bucket is in us-east-1. Tileset ids are at most 32 characters excluding the username, with only - and _ allowed. Names are at most 64 characters. Deleting an upload removes only the status record. Re-posting an existing tileset id replaces the data, but only for tilesets created by the Uploads API. Exceeding 60 requests/min returns 429.

verified.claim: 6. The Uploads API limit for TIFF/GeoTIFF is 10 GB, only 8-bit GeoTIFFs are supported, and the recommended prep is EPSG:3857, 256x256 blocks, LZW and no alpha.
verified.correction: The API page lists TIFF/GeoTIFF at 10 GB and MBTiles at 25 GB. The 8-bit restriction and the prep tips are on the troubleshooting page, not the API page. The MTS pricing guide confirms that the Uploads API (and Studio) picks the zoom levels and you cannot set maxzoom.

verified.claim: 7. An MTS raster recipe (type 'raster', version 1, minzoom/maxzoom required, colorinterp filters) accepts uint8, non-YCbCr GeoTIFF/COG that is panchromatic, RGB or RGBA, and outputs webp/png/jpg tiles usable as a GL JS raster source.
verified.correction: All points match the docs. Limits are 20 GB per file, up to 10 files and 50 GB per source. Publish is limited to 2 requests/min and creating a source to 100/min. Publishing an update to an existing tileset only shows new tiles as cached ones expire. The colorinterp value for a single-band panchromatic image is not documented; the docs show only red/green/blue and say filter order sets RGB channel order. CLI: mapbox-tilesets 2.2.0 (2026-01-07), requires Python >=3.10, command 'tilesets upload-raster-source ... [--replace]'.

verified.claim: 8. Tileset privacy can be changed with PATCH /tilesets/v1/{tileset_id} {private:false} (tilesets:write), and tilesets are private by default.
verified.correction: The create-tileset docs list 'private' with 'Default is true'. PATCH updates name, description, private and attribution. DELETE /tilesets/v1/{tileset_id} needs tilesets:write. Note that the Uploads API docs still say tilesets can only be deleted in Studio, while MTS documents a DELETE endpoint.

verified.claim: 9. Web map loads: 50,000/month free, then $5.00/$4.00/$3.00/$2.50 per 1,000. A map load includes unlimited Vector Tiles API and Raster Tiles API requests.
verified.correction: These are the exact numbers on the pricing page. Above 5M loads the page says to contact sales. Raster Tiles API: 750k free, then $0.25/$0.20/$0.15. Static Tiles API: 200k free, then $0.50/$0.40/$0.30. Vector Tiles API: 200k free, then $0.25/$0.20/$0.15.

verified.claim: 10. Tileset processing: 10,000 MB/month free, then $0.007/MB. 20 CUs free, then $0.90 (21–1,000), $0.85 and $0.80 per CU. Billed once per successful job or upload, for both MTS and the Uploads API.
verified.correction: Correction to the summary: the new model is not 'for tilesets since 2024-08-01'. The legacy guide says legacy km² pricing applies to 'existing tilesets users before August 1, 2024', which is account level, not tileset level. Check whether ventura86 is on legacy pricing. Under legacy pricing, maxzoom 17–22 is billed as 1 cm precision with area measured at z17, which is expensive for high-resolution imagery. CU guide: for maxzoom ≥11, sources of 200 MB–5 GB use about 5–30 CU and sources over 5 GB use 30+ CU. One uncropped high-resolution job can therefore exceed the 20 CU free tier.

verified.claim: 11. Tileset hosting is billed per tileset hosting day regardless of size. 750/month free, then $0.01370 (751–3,000), $0.01096, $0.00822, $0.00548 and $0.00274 per day.
verified.correction: These are the exact tiers. The guide states that file size does not affect hosting cost. Two additions: tilesets created before 2020-10-01 are exempt from hosting billing, and Mapbox default tilesets are exempt. The worked examples ($6.17 for 40 tilesets, about $30.8 for 100) are arithmetically correct.

verified.claim: 12. Accounts without a payment method are on a trial: 5,000 map loads, 1 GB and 10 CU of MTS processing, 75 hosting days, no Raster Tiles API, and one token that cannot be created, rotated or deleted.
verified.correction: All of this is confirmed. Mapbox now calls it 'demo access'. The researcher missed two harder facts. (a) 'When you reach a usage cap on demo access, you lose access to all Mapbox APIs until you upgrade', so the whole public site goes blank, not only the over-limit product. (b) Rate limits are lower. Two inferences: custom raster tilesets used through mapbox:// are served by the Raster Tiles API, which is unavailable on demo access, so the historical layers probably won't render at all. And with no way to create an sk token, CI can't call MTS or the Uploads API. The docs give no effective date and don't say whether accounts created before this tier existed are affected, so check the ventura86 Console status.

verified.claim: (Summary) Studio/Console GeoTIFF uploads are limited to 300 MB each and 20 per month, go through the Uploads API, and the Studio manual contradicts itself on billing.
verified.correction: The limits are confirmed: the Console Data Workbench table lists GeoTIFF at 300 MB, processed by the Uploads API, with a free limit of 20 uploads per month. I found no contradiction in the current Studio manual. reference/tilesets says 'Tilesets uploaded in Mapbox Studio are free, and do not incur processing or hosting charges' within 20 uploads per month and 300 MB each. Only 'MTS within Studio' (beta) may incur charges. I could not verify the researcher's 'Studio UI text'. If the docs are accurate, a manual Console upload of a GeoTIFF cropped to Bucharest and under 300 MB might avoid processing and hosting charges, but it cannot be automated from CI.

verified.claim: (Summary) Browser CORS: api.mapbox.com answers preflights for the Uploads credentials and MTS sources endpoints with ACAO, and the S3 bucket tilestream-tilesets-production allows PUT with the x-amz headers.
verified.correction: My own probes on 2026-10-11 reproduce this, with one caveat. Preflights without an access_token query parameter return 401 with no CORS headers. With ?access_token=... they return 204 with ACAO. Credentials echoes the origin; tilesets/sources returns '*'. 401 responses also carry ACAO. The S3 preflight returns ACAO *, allows PUT/POST/GET/HEAD and the authorization, x-amz-date, x-amz-content-sha256 and x-amz-security-token headers, and exposes ETag. It is still unconfirmed whether the credentials endpoint returns that bucket today, because that needs a real token. mapbox-sdk-js (0.16.2) docs say to pass a Blob in the browser for createTilesetSource. Every path still needs an sk token in the browser.

verified.claim: 13. URL restrictions: up to 100 URLs per token, only the domain is required, subdomains and subpaths allowed, paths case-sensitive, no wildcards or IPs, Referer required (no-referrer and same-origin unsupported), localhost must be listed, not allowed on the default public token.
verified.correction: Everything matches. Additional unsupported cases: privacy-blocking extensions such as Brave Shields and Ghostery, and the mobile SDKs. Mapbox calls URL restrictions 'best-effort'. Tokens API rate limit is 100 requests/min per account. Temporary tokens last at most 1 hour and 'can't be updated or revoked'. Their create body accepts only expires and scopes, so URL restrictions aren't supported (inferred from the parameter list). Whether a token is pk or sk is determined by its scopes, and a token cannot be given more scopes than the token that creates it.

verified.claim: 14. Browsers send only the origin as Referer on cross-origin requests by default, so restrict the token to https://ventura8.github.io and not the /bucurestiuldisparut.github.io path.
verified.correction: This is directly supported by the GL JS docs, not only Search JS. 'If you limit the referrer to the origin, make sure that the URL you restrict your access token to doesn't contain path information.' Since the browser default (strict-origin-when-cross-origin) sends only the origin cross-origin, restricting to the origin is correct. Also note that a CSP 'sandbox' directive needs allow-same-origin.

verified.claim: 15. GL JS has no addProtocol. v3.21.0 added the TileProvider API plus the official mapbox-gl-pmtiles-provider plugin loaded on demand, v3.23.0 added raster PMTiles, and the example uses a plain https .pmtiles URL.
verified.correction: Correct, with additions. The 3.32.0 TypeScript typings mark TileProvider and addTileProvider '@experimental' and '@private', i.e. subject to change. The bundled default provider is api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/plugins/mapbox-gl-pmtiles-provider/v0.0.2/mapbox-gl-pmtiles-provider.js (HTTP 200). The docs say .pmtiles detection by extension applies to vector sources, but a GL JS render test (tile-providers/pmtiles-raster-overscale) uses {type:'raster', url:'...pmtiles'}, which supports the raster inference. 3.32.0 fixed transformRequest headers being dropped on PMTiles requests.

verified.claim: 16. GL JS v3 bills a map load on every Map initialisation regardless of tile source.
verified.correction: Confirmed: 'A map load occurs whenever a Mapbox GL JS Map object is initialized', with a maximum 12-hour session. Consequence the researcher missed: mapbox-gl-compare needs two Map instances (beforeMap and afterMap), so every swipe view costs 2 map loads. On demo access that leaves about 2,500 compare page views per month before all APIs are cut off.

verified.claim: 17. GitHub Pages: published site ≤1 GB, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10-minute deploy timeout, ACAO:* and HTTP 206 for Range requests.
verified.correction: The docs confirm all three limits, plus the soft limit of 10 builds per hour, which doesn't apply to custom Actions workflows. My curl to ventura8.github.io returned access-control-allow-origin: * and, with a Range header, HTTP 206 with a content-range.

verified.claim: 18. GitHub Release asset downloads redirect to a host without CORS headers, so browsers can't read PMTiles from Releases directly.
verified.correction: Confirmed by a direct test, not only third-party posts. github.com/.../releases/download returns a 302 with no ACAO, to release-assets.githubusercontent.com, which also returns no ACAO (it does honour Range with 206). GitHub docs confirm under 2 GiB per asset, up to 1,000 assets per release, and no limit on total size or bandwidth.

verified.claim: (Summary) GDAL's PMTiles driver (3.8+) is vector-only; for raster use MBTiles, then gdaladdo, then pmtiles convert.
verified.correction: True for released GDAL: the latest is 3.13.3 (2026-08-18). GDAL master already documents a raster PMTiles driver with read and CreateCopy support for PNG/JPEG/WEBP tiles, marked 'versionadded:: 3.14', which is unreleased and expected around Nov 2026. It also offers a direct 'gdal raster convert in.mbtiles out.pmtiles'. The MBTiles + gdaladdo + pmtiles convert pipeline remains correct for now.

verified.claim: (Summary) Cloudflare R2 offers 10 GB-month, 1M Class A and 10M Class B operations free, then $0.015/GB-month, $4.50 and $0.36 per million, with free egress.
verified.correction: The numbers match the official pricing page, and the free tier applies only to Standard storage. I did not verify the 'payment method required' point from a primary source.

verified.claim: (Summary) USGS-purchased declassified imagery is US-government public domain, so public tilesets are fine.
verified.correction: USGS EROS lists the declassified CORONA imagery with 'Sources/Usage: Public Domain'. It was declassified by EO 12951 (1995). Citing USGS EROS as the source is still good practice.

verified.claim: (Concrete) Max zoom from resolution: 156543.03·cos(44.43°)/2^z gives z15 ≈ 3.41 m, z16 ≈ 1.71 m, z17 ≈ 0.85 m, z18 ≈ 0.43 m.
verified.correction: The arithmetic is correct (cos 44.43° ≈ 0.714). The MTS raster recipe requires explicit minzoom and maxzoom and points to the zoom-level/resolution glossary. Higher maxzoom raises CU cost sharply (the pricing guide warns about maxzoom ≥11 and ≥14), so prefer the lowest maxzoom that preserves detail.

verification.missed_important_points:
1) The current repo uses no ventura86 resources. index.html, interactiv.html and index-l.html contain pk tokens whose payloads decode to the users 'fostulbucuresti' and 'razvanr'. index.html loads the style mapbox://styles/fostulbucuresti/... and five fostulbucuresti.* tilesets on GL JS v2.6.1, and index-l.html uses mapbox.js v2.2.2. Since the user will not use fostulbucuresti resources, the rewrite must replace every token, style and tileset with ventura86 equivalents. The swap must not keep billing or depending on other people's accounts. (Verified by grepping /home/sergiu-alexandrescu/Projects/bucurestiuldisparut.github.io/index.html, interactiv.html and index-l.html.)

2) Demo access is a hard kill switch. On reaching any usage cap, 'you lose access to all Mapbox APIs until you upgrade' (https://docs.mapbox.com/accounts/guides/demo-access.md). Also, the Raster Tiles API (which serves mapbox:// raster tilesets) is unavailable and no sk token can be created. Without a card, the whole Mapbox-hosted raster pipeline (MTS or Uploads from CI, and public display of the raster tilesets) probably cannot work at all, not just at reduced quota. The Mapbox architecture depends on the user adding a card to ventura86, the same blocker as Firebase Blaze. Check ventura86's Console status first; an older account may already be on standard access, but the docs don't say.

3) The swipe-compare UI doubles billing. mapbox-gl-compare requires two Map objects, and each Map init is one billable map load (12-hour session). A single-map design (opacity slider, or a layer toggle in one Map) halves map loads. Don't re-create Map objects when switching city or epoch.

4) There is a license-clean, card-free alternative the researcher only mentioned in passing: MapLibre GL JS (6.14.0, BSD-3-Clause) plus the pmtiles JS library (4.5.0, BSD-3-Clause). MapLibre supports raster PMTiles officially via addProtocol (https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/maplibre). It has no map-load billing, no Mapbox account and no token. With PMTiles on GitHub Pages (≤1 GB, CORS and Range verified) or R2, this removes Mapbox from the critical path. Trade-off: no Mapbox Standard basemap, so a free OSM-based basemap (for example Protomaps) is needed. Since GL JS v3 bills map loads even with self-hosted PMTiles, the 'self-host on Pages' fallback only saves money if the renderer is also switched. This is the main architecture fork to decide early.

5) The TileProvider and PMTiles path in Mapbox GL JS is marked @experimental and @private in the 3.32.0 typings, and raster-allow-draping is missing from the 3.31+ builds despite the changelog. Pin GL JS exactly and test before depending on either.

6) Cost control for MTS raster jobs. Processing MB is the tileset source size, and CU grows with source size and maxzoom (≥11, and especially ≥14). Uncropped USGS film scans will blow through the 20 CU and 10 GB free tier. Crop to the Bucharest area, reproject to EPSG:3857 and compress before upload. Mosaic multiple frames of one epoch into one tileset (a source holds up to 10 files and 50 GB) to keep hosting days down, since each tileset is billed per day regardless of size.

7) Check whether ventura86 is on legacy km² tileset pricing (accounts that used tilesets before 2024-08-01). Under legacy pricing, maxzoom 17+ counts as 1 cm precision and is much more expensive.

8) A Console/Studio manual upload might be free. Current docs say GeoTIFF uploads of ≤300 MB, ≤20 per month, through the Console/Studio (Uploads API under the hood) incur no processing or hosting charges. Cropped city-scale scans may fit, but this path is manual (not CI) and unverified against the live UI.

9) Browser-side uploads are technically CORS-capable, but only with access_token in the query string (preflights without it return 401 with no CORS headers). Minting temporary tk tokens also needs an sk token with tokens:write on a server. With no backend (no Blaze), the realistic secure options are a GitHub Actions workflow holding the sk token as a secret, or the admin pasting an sk token into the admin page at runtime and keeping it in memory only.

10) Standard style 'middle' sits behind 3D buildings, and draped rasters render under all symbols on globe or terrain. Modern 3D buildings and landmarks will cover 1960s imagery unless they are disabled through Standard style config (inference, not verified).

research.area: Firebase (Spark vs Blaze, Firestore, Auth, JS SDK via CDN, rules/indexes, CLI/CI auth, service accounts/WIF) for a static GitHub Pages front-end plus admin page, and free alternatives for photo storage. Checked against current docs as of 2026-10-11.
research.summary:
BOTTOM LINE: The project can stay on the no-cost Spark plan if it uses only Firestore and Auth. Cloud Storage for Firebase, Cloud Functions (every generation), Secret Manager and scheduled functions all need a linked Cloud Billing account, which means Blaze. Photos therefore have to live somewhere outside Firebase. Heavy or privileged work (GDAL, Mapbox upload, writing to Firestore with a service account) has to run in GitHub Actions using a service-account key stored as a secret. The user's instruction to buy imagery from USGS instead of using fostulbucuresti does not change the Firebase design. It does mean the raw scans, which can be large, will never fit in Firestore (1 MiB per document) or in a git repo (100 MiB per file). Keep them in GitHub Releases (each file under 2 GiB) or have the Actions run fetch them, and send only the finished tiles to Mapbox.

1) SPARK VS BLAZE (verified from docs)
- Cloud Storage for Firebase is not available on Spark. The pricing page shows "Not applicable" in every Spark row.
- Since Oct 30 2024, creating a new default bucket (named <project>.firebasestorage.app) requires Blaze.
- From Feb 3 2026, even old *.appspot.com buckets require Blaze. Spark projects lose read/write access (402/403 errors) and the buckets disappear from the console.
- Cloud Functions: "to deploy functions, your project must be on the Blaze pricing plan." This applies to all generations. Only the local emulator works on Spark.
- Scheduled functions also use Cloud Scheduler, which costs $0.10 per job per month, with 3 free jobs per Google account.
- Secret Manager is a Google Cloud product. Google Cloud's Free Tier "requires a billing account," so Secret Manager effectively needs Blaze. Its free amounts are 6 active secret versions and 10K access operations per month.
- Firestore Standard edition, on both plans: 1 GiB stored, 50K reads, 20K writes and 20K deletes per day (reset around midnight Pacific time), and 10 GiB per month of network egress.
- Only one database per project gets the free tier. Additional databases need Blaze.
- Composite indexes: 200 per database without billing, 1000 with billing.
- Auth: 50K monthly active users at no cost on both plans. Google sign-in is free.
- Auth limits on Spark (for projects with Identity Platform): 3,000 daily active users (Tier 1), 100 new accounts per hour per IP, 150 password-reset emails per day. None of these matter for a single admin.
- Firebase Hosting is available on Spark but is not needed here.

2) BLAZE NO-COST AMOUNTS (verified)
- Storage buckets created after Oct 2024 (*.firebasestorage.app):
  - 5 GB-months stored, 100 GB downloaded per month, 5K uploads and 50K downloads per month.
  - These free amounts apply only in us-central1, us-west1 and us-east1, so a bucket in Europe would be billed from the first byte.
- Old *.appspot.com buckets: 5 GB stored, 1 GB per day downloaded, 20K uploads and 50K downloads per day.
- Functions: 2M invocations, 400K GB-seconds, 200K CPU-seconds and 5 GB egress per month.
  - The Firebase pricing page also lists 120 Cloud Build minutes per day.
  - Google Cloud's free-tier page instead says 2,500 build-minutes per month on e2-standard-2 and 0.5 GB of Artifact Registry. The two sources disagree.
- Budget alerts:
  - When upgrading in the Firebase console you are prompted to create an alerts-only budget. You can also create one in Cloud Billing > Budgets.
  - Alerts do not cap spending.
- Spend caps, which pause a service at 100% of its budget for the rest of the month, exist only for Firebase AI Logic, App Hosting, Cloud Functions and Extensions. They do not cover Storage or Firestore.
- Linking a billing account automatically moves the project to Blaze. The user has to enter payment details themselves; the Free Trial needs a card or other payment method.
- The $300 trial credit may apply to new users.

3) JS SDK (verified)
- The latest Firebase JS SDK is 13.0.0, released Oct 7 2026. The npm "latest" tag also points to 13.0.0. The previous version was 12.19.0 (Sep 9 2026).
- The 13.0.0 breaking changes are almost all in AI Logic. Firestore added BSON types and typing fixes. No Auth breaking changes are listed.
- 12.0.0 (Jul 17 2025) moved the build target to ES2020, required Node 20+, and removed firebase/vertexai.
- The official way to use the SDK without a bundler (docs.firebase "alt-setup") is a `<script type="module">` that imports from https://www.gstatic.com/firebasejs/13.0.0/firebase-app.js, firebase-auth.js and firebase-firestore.js. Firebase still "strongly recommends" npm for most apps.
- FirebaseUI:
  - v6 is the old line and only works with the compat (namespaced) SDK.
  - The new line is the `@firebase-oss/ui-*` packages (React, Angular and Shadcn on a framework-agnostic core). They install from npm with the @beta tag, and the docs show no CDN build.
  - For one admin, a single button that calls signInWithPopup(auth, new GoogleAuthProvider()) is simpler.
- Sign-in on github.io:
  - signInWithRedirect breaks on browsers that block third-party storage (Chrome M115+ since Jun 24 2024, Firefox 109+, Safari 16.1+) when the app runs on a domain other than firebaseapp.com.
  - Switching to signInWithPopup is the documented Option 2 and fits github.io best.
  - Add the domain under Security > Authentication > Settings > Authorized domains.
  - localhost is authorized by default.

4) RULES AND INDEXES (verified)
- Rules can check admin status in two ways:
  - Read another document: exists() or get() on /databases/$(database)/documents/admins/$(request.auth.uid). Each such call is a billed read, even when the rule denies the request. The limit is 10 calls for single-document requests and queries, and 20 for transactions and batches.
  - Use custom claims: request.auth.token.admin == true. Claims are set only with the Admin SDK (setCustomUserClaims / set_custom_user_claims), are limited to 1000 bytes, and reach the user after a token refresh (getIdToken(true)).
- Validate incoming data through request.resource.data.
- "Rules are not filters": public queries must include where('published','==',true), otherwise a rule based on resource.data.published rejects the whole query.
- Equality-only queries are served by single-field indexes. A query like where(cityId ==) + where(published ==) + orderBy(year) needs a composite index on cityId ASC, published ASC, year ASC.

5) CONSOLE SETUP AND CLI (verified; the console menus were reorganized)
- Create the project: the user must accept the Firebase terms. Gemini in Firebase and Google Analytics are optional; I recommend leaving Analytics off.
- Add a web app (a nickname is required) and copy the firebaseConfig.
- The Firebase API key is "public by design." New keys have been auto-restricted to Firebase APIs since May 2024.
- Create Firestore under Databases & Storage > Firestore > Create database:
  - Standard edition is the default.
  - The location is permanent. Options include multi-region eur3 (europe-west1/europe-west4), europe-west3 (Frankfurt) or europe-central2 (Warsaw). There is no Romanian region.
  - Choose production mode.
- Enable Google under Security > Authentication > Sign-in method.
- CLI: firebase-tools is at 15.33.0 and needs Node 20 or newer.
  - Token login (login:ci, --token or FIREBASE_TOKEN) is marked "DEPRECATED ... will be removed in a future major version."
  - The documented CI method is GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS pointing to a service-account JSON key, then `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,firestore:indexes --project <id>`.

6) GITHUB ACTIONS ACCESS TO FIRESTORE
- Admin SDK versions: firebase-admin for Node is 14.5.0 (needs Node 22 or newer); for Python it is 7.7.0 (needs Python 3.9 or newer; 3.10+ recommended).
- Setup: generate a key under Project settings > Service accounts > Generate new private key. Store it in a GitHub secret, write it to a file in the job, set GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, then call firebase_admin.initialize_app() or initializeApp({credential: applicationDefault()}).
- Key-creation restrictions: Google's "secure by default" organization policies, including constraints/iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation, are enforced for Organizations created on or after May 3 2024.
  - Organizations are auto-created for a *domain*, either when a domain user first logs in or when someone creates a billing account with no organization.
  - My inference: a personal @gmail.com project has "No organization," so key creation is not blocked. The docs do not say this directly.
- Keyless alternative, Workload Identity Federation (WIF) with GitHub OIDC:
  - Use google-github-actions/auth@v3 with `permissions: id-token: write`.
  - Its README warns: "This option is not supported by Firebase Admin SDK. Use Service Account Key JSON authentication instead."
  - But firebase-admin-node issue #1377 was resolved by PR #2466 (move to google-auth-library). According to secondary sources, firebase-admin 13+ accepts external_account credentials, with some permission problems reported in discussion #2816.
  - Conclusion: use a key first. WIF is optional hardening, for example with the plain google-cloud-firestore client library.

7) PHOTO STORAGE WITHOUT FIREBASE STORAGE (verified limits)
- GitHub repository:
  - Warning at 50 MiB per file; files over 100 MiB are blocked; browser uploads are limited to 25 MiB.
  - Recommended repo size is under 1 GB, and strongly under 5 GB.
  - A published Pages site is limited to 1 GB, with a soft 100 GB per month of bandwidth and a 10-minute deploy timeout.
  - The Contents API (PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/{path}) needs the repo scope or Contents:write. Calls must be made one at a time, because parallel calls conflict.
- GitHub Releases: up to 1000 assets per release, each under 2 GiB, with no limit on total size or bandwidth.
- Cloudinary Free: 25 credits per month (1 credit = 1 GB storage, 1 GB bandwidth or 1K transformations) and no card required. The 10 MB image limit comes from Cloudinary support posts, not the pricing page.
- ImgBB: free API with a key, 32 MB per image, optional expiration. No SLA is stated.
- Cloudflare R2: 10 GB-month storage, 1M Class A and 10M Class B operations per month, and free egress. The docs require completing the checkout flow to add an R2 subscription; community reports say this asks for a payment method.
- Firestore can technically hold small images: 1 MiB per document, 1,048,487 bytes per field, stored as a Bytes field or base64 (about +33%). Each image counts as a read and against the 10 GiB per month egress. That is acceptable only for tiny thumbnails.

KEY INFERENCE ABOUT READ BUDGET
50K reads per day runs out quickly if every visitor queries all photo documents: 500 photos means about 100 visitors per day. Two fixes:
- Have a GitHub Action publish a static JSON file or Firestore data bundle (loadBundle + namedQuery + getDocsFromCache) to Pages or jsDelivr, so public visitors do not query Firestore at all.
- Or keep one manifest document per city.

research.recommendation:
1. Stay on Spark and use only Firestore (Standard edition, location eur3 or europe-central2) plus Auth (Google provider, signInWithPopup, ventura8.github.io added as an authorized domain). Do not plan on Cloud Storage, Cloud Functions, Secret Manager or scheduled functions; all of them need a billing account that the user would have to add.

2. Admin authorization: an /admins/{uid} document created by hand in the console, checked with exists() in the rules. Optionally also set an admin custom claim once from an Action using the Admin SDK, so the rules can check request.auth.token.admin without an extra read.

3. Public reads: every query must filter on published==true, with a composite index on cityId+published+year deployed from firestore.indexes.json.

4. To protect the 50K reads per day, have a GitHub Action, triggered by the admin's "publish" button through repository_dispatch, export the published data as a static JSON file or Firestore bundle to GitHub Pages or jsDelivr. The public map engine then loads that and never needs the Firestore SDK; only the admin page loads Firebase from gstatic.

5. Pin the SDK to firebasejs/13.0.0, or 12.19.0 for a conservative choice, with all imports on the same version. Skip FirebaseUI.

6. Photos: client-side WebP resize, then commit through the GitHub Contents API into a dedicated public media repo, served by Pages or jsDelivr pinned to a commit. Keep raw USGS purchases in GitHub Releases of a data repo (each under 2 GiB), and let Actions run GDAL and push tiles to Mapbox. Cloudinary Free (no card) is the fallback if upload-time transformations are wanted. Avoid R2 (needs a subscription checkout, likely a card) and Firestore-embedded images (except tiny thumbnails).

7. CI: one service account (the firebase-adminsdk key, or a dedicated SA with datastore.user, firebaserules.admin, datastore.indexAdmin and serviceUsageConsumer) as a JSON key in a GitHub secret, used through GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. Use firebase-tools 15.33.0 on Node 22 for rules and index deploys, and firebase-admin 7.7.0 (Python) or 14.5.0 (Node) for data. Do not use FIREBASE_TOKEN. Treat WIF as a later hardening step and test it, since the Admin SDK's support is contested.

8. The user must personally accept the Firebase terms and choose the support email. They should enter payment details only if they later decide to move to Blaze, and should set a budget alert at that point, keeping in mind that alerts do not cap spending for Storage or Firestore.

verification.area: firebase (Spark vs Blaze, Firestore and Auth on github.io, CI access from GitHub Actions, photo and scan storage outside Firebase)

verified.claim: 1. Cloud Storage for Firebase is unavailable on Spark (every Spark row on the pricing page says 'Not applicable'). Provisioning a new default bucket (<id>.firebasestorage.app) has required Blaze since Oct 30 2024.
verified.correction: Confirmed. The pricing page lists 'Not applicable' for every Spark Storage row. The locations page says that starting Oct 30 2024, newly provisioned default buckets use *.firebasestorage.app. The FAQ says provisioning a new default bucket requires Blaze. The Blaze no-cost amounts (5 GB-months stored, 100 GB/month downloaded, 5K uploads/month, 50K downloads/month) apply only to us-central1, us-west1 and us-east1, which is also confirmed.

verified.claim: 2. Keeping access to existing *.appspot.com buckets has required Blaze since February 03 2026. Spark projects get 402/403 errors and lose console access; the data is kept but cannot be accessed.
verified.correction: The FAQ says the requirement 'went into effect starting February 03, 2026'. It quotes a 402 message: 'Cloud Storage for Firebase no longer supports Firebase projects that are on the no-cost Spark pricing plan'. Buckets are hidden in both the Firebase and Google Cloud consoles, and the data stays in place but cannot be accessed until the project upgrades.

verified.claim: 3. Deploying Cloud Functions requires Blaze for all generations; only the emulator works on Spark. After a downgrade you cannot deploy new or existing functions.
verified.correction: The functions page says: 'You can emulate functions in any Firebase project, but to deploy functions, your project must be on the Blaze pricing plan.' The pricing-plans page says that after a downgrade you 'can't deploy new or existing Cloud Functions'. The pricing page shows 'Not applicable' for every Spark Functions row. Neither page mentions generations explicitly, but the requirement is stated generally.

verified.claim: 4. Firestore Standard no-cost quota on Spark and Blaze: 1 GiB stored, 50K reads, 20K writes and 20K deletes per day, 10 GiB/month egress. Resets around midnight Pacific. One free database per project.
verified.correction: All confirmed; the quotas page says 'exactly one free database per project'. Two additions. Enterprise edition also has a no-cost tier on Spark, measured in different units (40K write units, 50K read units and 50K real-time update units per day), but the docs list data bundles only under Standard, so Standard remains the right choice. The pricing-plans page also says that on Spark, a product that goes over its no-cost quota is shut off for all apps in the project.

verified.claim: 5. Maximum document size 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes); maximum field value 1,048,487 bytes; 200 composite indexes per database without billing, 1000 with billing.
verified.correction: Confirmed. Also relevant: maximum API request size is 10 MiB, and transactions time out at 270 s.

verified.claim: 6. The latest Firebase JS SDK is 13.0.0 (Oct 7 2026; npm latest). Its breaking changes are AI Logic only. 12.0.0 targets ES2020, needs Node 20+ and removed firebase/vertexai.
verified.correction: npm 'latest' is 13.0.0, and the release notes list 13.0.0 on Oct 7 2026, 12.19.0 on Sep 9 2026 and 12.18.0 on Aug 19 2026. Every 13.0.0 breaking change listed is in AI Logic; none affects Auth, Firestore or the core app. The 12.0.0 notes match the claim.

verified.correction: The alt-setup page currently shows the 13.0.0 gstatic URLs for app, analytics, auth and firestore, and says 'For most Firebase web apps we strongly recommend using the SDK via npm.'

verified.claim: 8. On apps hosted outside firebaseapp.com (such as github.io), signInWithRedirect breaks on browsers that block third-party storage (Chrome M115+ from Jun 24 2024, Firefox 109+, Safari 16.1+). signInWithPopup is documented Option 2.
verified.correction: Confirmed. The page also warns that 'popups are occasionally blocked by the device or platform'. It does not discuss COOP. In practice GitHub Pages does not send a COOP header, so popups should work.

verified.claim: 9. Authorized domains are added under Security > Authentication > Settings > Authorized domains. Without it sign-in fails with auth/unauthorized-domain. localhost is authorized by default.
verified.correction: The localhost part is wrong for a new project. The Auth FAQ says: 'In projects created after April 28, 2025, Firebase Authentication no longer includes localhost as an authorized domain by default.' If the user wants local testing, they must add localhost by hand (Settings tab > Authorized Domains > Add domain). Google 'strongly discourages' localhost in production projects. verified.correction: The page says 'security rules are not filters—queries are all or nothing' and gives the published==true example.

verified.correction: The docs' own example is country == 'USA' with orderBy('population'), which 'would need a manual index'.

The README also says GitHub packages over 150 MB or single files over 20 MB 'are not supported by default'. A growing photo repo (for example 500 photos x 500 KB = 250 MB) passes 150 MB. verified.correction: Spark Hosting is real: 10 GB storage and 360 MB/day transfer at no cost. Whether it is 'not needed' is a judgment, and it overlooks two benefits. It can also hold photos or bundles (10 GB), though 360 MB/day is much less bandwidth than Pages' soft 100 GB/month. Deploying Hosting from Actions works with the same service account.

verification.missed_important_points:
Points the researcher missed that would change the architecture. All are verified unless marked INFERENCE.

(1) localhost is no longer authorized by default. For Firebase projects created after April 28, 2025, local admin testing fails until the user adds localhost under Authentication > Settings > Authorized Domains. Source: https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/faq-and-troubleshooting

(2) Standalone organizations may block service-account keys.
- Google now auto-creates a 'standalone organization' for new Google Cloud Free Trial customers, including Gmail users, when they accept the Cloud terms. An org is also auto-created when a billing account is created with no org.
- Orgs created on or after May 3 2024 enforce iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation.
- INFERENCE: if the user ever signs up for the Cloud Free Trial or creates a billing account (for example to go Blaze), key creation may be blocked for projects under that org. Generate the key while the project is still under 'No organization', or plan WIF as the fallback.
- WIF is now viable for the Admin SDK: firebase-admin-node 13+ accepts external_account (issue #1377 closed by PR #2466; maintainer confirmed in v13). Python firebase-admin uses google-auth ADC, but that is unverified here.
- Sources: https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/standalone-organization-overview ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/secure-by-default-organizations ; https://github.com/firebase/firebase-admin-node/issues/1377

(3) Shared-origin security risk on github.io.
- The site is served at ventura8.github.io/bucurestiuldisparut.github.io/, so its origin is https://ventura8.github.io. Every other ventura8 project Pages site shares that origin.
- Firebase says 'Firebase Auth web sessions are single host origin', and localStorage is per origin.
- INFERENCE: the admin's Firebase session and a GitHub PAT kept in localStorage are readable by script on any ventura8.github.io project site, through XSS or a compromised dependency.
- Mitigations: give the admin page its own origin (Firebase Hosting <project>.web.app on Spark, or a custom domain), or keep the PAT out of the browser. One way is for the admin to write images as base64 chunks under 1 MiB to a 'pending' Firestore collection, then have an Action using the service-account key move them into the media repo and delete them.
- Source: https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/web/auth-state-persistence

(4) GitHub Release assets are not CORS-enabled. I checked live: the github.com/.../releases/download 302 carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Releases can hold raw USGS scans for Actions (curl), but never browser-loaded images, tiles or Mapbox GL image sources. GitHub Pages and raw.githubusercontent.com do return 'access-control-allow-origin: *' (checked with curl -I).

(5) jsDelivr cannot serve the photo library.
- Its Terms of Use prohibit general-purpose media or image hosting.
- GitHub packages over 150 MB, or single files over 20 MB, are not supported by default. HTML is served as text/plain.
- Use jsDelivr only for the engine bundle (tagged releases).
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsdelivr/jsdelivr/master/Terms%20of%20Use.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jsdelivr/jsdelivr/master/README.md

(6) Abuse of the public read quota. On Spark, a product that goes over its no-cost quota is shut off for all apps in the project. One bad actor running 50K reads would block the admin's own reads too.
- Preferred fix: serve visitors a static JSON file or bundle so they never touch Firestore.
- Optionally add App Check. Firestore enforcement is supported, and reCAPTCHA Enterprise includes 10K assessments per month at no cost.
- Also restrict list queries in rules (for example request.query.limit).
- Sources: https://firebase.google.com/docs/projects/billing/firebase-pricing-plans ; https://firebase.google.com/docs/app-check/web/recaptcha-provider ; https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/security/rules-query

(7) Scheduled workflows go dormant. In public repos, scheduled workflows are automatically disabled after 60 days without repository activity. Rebuild the public JSON or bundle on repository_dispatch or workflow_dispatch, triggered by the admin; that also needs Contents:write. Do not rely on cron alone. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows

(8) USGS purchase and processing realities, given the user's decision to buy imagery from USGS rather than use fostulbucuresti.
- USGS on-demand scanning costs $30 per CORONA frame or Hexagon scene, at 7-micron or 14-micron resolution, with no geocorrection.
- The M2M API's password 'login' endpoint was scheduled for deprecation on Feb 26 2025, replaced by application tokens via login-token. Store the ERS application token as a GitHub secret if Actions download automatically.
- Public-repo standard Linux runners have 4 CPU, 16 GB RAM and 14 GB SSD.
- INFERENCE: 7-micron Hexagon or KH-4 frames can run to several GB each. They may need splitting to stay under 2 GiB per Release asset, and GDAL intermediates can fill the 14 GB disk, so process one frame per job and clean up between steps.
- Sources: https://www.usgs.gov/centers/eros/science/usgs-eros-archive-declassified-data-declassified-satellite-imagery-1 ; https://www.usgs.gov/centers/eros/science/usgs-eros-archive-declassified-data-declassified-satellite-imagery-3 ; https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/m2m-application-token-documentation ; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners

(9) WIF token lifetime. Impersonated access tokens last 1 hour by default, not 5 to 10 minutes; long GDAL jobs should re-authenticate or use impersonation. Source: https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth

(10) Choose Firestore Standard explicitly. Enterprise also has a Spark free tier, but it does not auto-create single-field indexes and the docs list data bundles only under Standard. Source: https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/editions

(11) Firestore location may already be fixed. If the project's default Google Cloud resource location is already set, the console will not offer a location choice for Firestore. Source: https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/quickstart

research.area: Engine delivery + CI automation (jsDelivr, Vite, GitHub Pages, GitHub Actions), current as of 2026-10-11
research.summary:
I checked the claims below against official docs, current release and registry data, and live HTTP headers on 2026-10-11. Anything marked INFERENCE is my own conclusion, not something the docs state.

Repo state (checked with read-only `gh api` and the local clone): `ventura8/bucurestiuldisparut.github.io` is public. Its default branch is `master`. Pages is currently `build_type: "legacy"`, serving from master at `/`, with HTTPS enforced. The git pack is 47 MiB, and `photos/` is 46 MB in the working tree. `photos/Ferdinand.png` is 29.5 MB. That is over jsDelivr's 20 MB per-file limit for GitHub content and over GitHub's 25 MiB limit for browser uploads. There are no workflows, no `.gitattributes` (so no LFS), and there is a `.nojekyll` file.

1) jsDelivr (/gh/)
- URL shape is `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/user/repo@version/file`. The version can be an exact tag, a full commit SHA, a branch, a semver range (`@1`, `@1.2`), or `@latest`/no version. With no tags, latest falls back to the default branch.
- Ranges only work with valid semver tags. I verified a leading `v` is stripped: tag `v5.3.8` resolves as `5.3.8`, and `@5` and `@latest` resolve to 5.3.8 rather than 6.0.0-alpha.1.
- If a file is missing from the newest release, a range serves it from an older release.
- Cache times per the README: exact versions and commits are effectively permanent (1-year headers plus permanent S3 storage, never updatable). Ranges and `@latest` are 7 days. Branches are 12 hours.
- Live headers today: exact versions send `max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable`. Ranges, `@latest` and branches all send `max-age=604800, s-maxage=43200` (7 days in the browser, 12 hours at the CDN). So purging the CDN does not clear browsers that already cached a range URL.
- Purge: the README says API access is granted by emailing d@jsdelivr.com. It is rate-limited, only works for alias URLs with valid semver, and does not affect exact versions. There is also a public web tool with reCAPTCHA at jsdelivr.com/tools/purge, backed by purge.jsdelivr.net. In practice `https://purge.jsdelivr.net/<same path>` answers unauthenticated requests, but that is not documented, so treat it as best effort.
- Limits: the README says packages over 150 MB and single files over 20 MB (for GitHub) are not supported by default. A real 403 error message reads "Package size exceeded the configured limit of 150 MB".
- The Terms of Use (effective 2026-10-05) set soft limits of 10,000 actively accessed files and 100,000 total files per repo. They prohibit using jsDelivr as general-purpose file or media hosting, for example "running an image hosting website".
- INFERENCE: for /gh/, the "package" is the whole repo at that ref, so a growing photo collection in the engine's repo could eventually break every new engine version. Put the engine in its own repo. Media should never be served through jsDelivr.
- npm alternative: `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pkg@1/file` caches the same way. unpkg redirects a range to the exact version (302 with `max-age=60, s-maxage=300`), so new releases reach users within minutes.
- npm publishing changed in 2025:
  - Classic tokens were revoked on 2025-12-09.
  - Granular tokens with write access now last at most 90 days and require 2FA by default.
  - Trusted publishing (OIDC) needs npm CLI 11.5.1+ and Node 22.14.0+, plus `permissions: id-token: write`. Provenance is generated automatically when a public repo publishes a public package.

2) Vite
- The current major is Vite 8: 8.0.0 shipped 2026-03-12 and the latest is 8.3.4. It uses Rolldown as its single bundler and needs Node 20.19+ or 22.12+.
- `build.rollupOptions` was renamed `build.rolldownOptions` (the old name is deprecated and still works for now).
- `build.lib` options:
  - Default formats are `['es','umd']`.
  - `name` is required for `iife` and `umd`.
  - `cssFileName` was added in Vite 6. Vite 5 always wrote `style.css`. From Vite 6 the CSS file defaults to the `fileName` string, or to the package.json `name` if `fileName` is a function.
  - In lib mode `cssCodeSplit` defaults to false, so you get one CSS file.
  - Lib mode does not replace `process.env.*`.
- Vite 8 behaviour changes that matter here:
  - `import.meta.url` becomes `undefined` in UMD and IIFE output.
  - Oxc is the default JS minifier and Lightning CSS the default CSS minifier.
  - The default target is baseline-widely-available (chrome111, edge111, firefox114, safari16.4, ios16.4).
- Mapbox GL JS (3.32.0) is licensed under the Mapbox TOS "for use only with" Mapbox products, and its npm package unpacks to about 67 MB. Externalize it as the global `mapboxgl` and load it from api.mapbox.com.
- Bundle the modular Firebase SDK. Firebase 13.0.0 shipped 2026-10-07; its breaking changes only affect AI Logic. The last 12.x is 12.19.0.

3) GitHub Pages
- Limits: a published site can be at most 1 GB, and the source repo is recommended to stay under 1 GB. Deployments time out after 10 minutes. The soft cap of 10 builds per hour does not apply to custom workflows. Bandwidth has a soft limit of 100 GB/month, and rate limiting returns 429. The artifact must be a gzip tar under 10 GB with no symlinks or hard links.
- The deploy job needs `pages: write` and `id-token: write`, plus the `github-pages` environment.
- Latest action releases are checkout v7.0.1, configure-pages v6.0.0, upload-pages-artifact v5.0.0 and deploy-pages v5.0.1. The docs example still shows older majors (checkout@v6, configure-pages@v5, upload-pages-artifact@v4, deploy-pages@v4).
- Since upload-pages-artifact v4, dotfiles are excluded by default (v5 adds `include-hidden-files`).
- Switching to Actions builds is a `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pages` with `build_type: "workflow"`. It needs a repo admin, and fine-grained tokens need both Administration: write and Pages: write.
- Pages responses send `cache-control: max-age=600` and `access-control-allow-origin: *`.

4) Runners
- Docs for public repos: `ubuntu-latest` and arm64 runners have 4 CPU, 16 GB RAM and a documented 14 GB SSD.
- A runner-images maintainer said on 2026-08-05 that public repos run on a 4-core VM with a 150 GB disk and about 90 GB free (fixed on 27 July 2026). Private repos get 75 GB with about 14 GB free. Only 14 GB is guaranteed.
- Limits: 6 hours per job, 35 days per workflow run, 20 concurrent jobs, a 10 GB cache per repo, and 1,000 GITHUB_TOKEN API requests per hour per repo. Actions are free for public repos on standard runners.
- `ubuntu-latest` is 24.04 today and moves to 26.04 gradually between Oct 19 and Nov 19, 2026. That also changes the apt `gdal-bin` version from 3.8.4 (24.04) to 3.12.2 (26.04).
- Upstream GDAL is at 3.13.3 (released 2026-08-18). The official images are on ghcr.io: `ubuntu-small` (about 385 MB, includes GDAL Python) and `ubuntu-full` (about 1.48 GB). The Docker Hub `osgeo/gdal` repo is stale; its newest tags are 3.6.3 from 2023.
- `ubuntu-slim` (1 vCPU, 5 GB RAM, 15-minute job cap, generally available since 2026-01-22) is good for small dispatch, purge or poll jobs.

5) Triggering workflows
- `workflow_dispatch` needs a fine-grained token with Actions: write. Inputs are capped at 25 properties and 65,535 characters, and the workflow file must exist on the default branch.
  - API version 2026-03-10: the call always returns 200 with `workflow_run_id`, `run_url` and `html_url`.
  - Default version 2022-11-28: it returns 204, unless you send `return_run_details: true` (added 2026-02-19).
- `repository_dispatch` needs Contents: write, returns 204 and always runs on the default branch. `event_type` is at most 100 characters; `client_payload` allows at most 10 top-level keys and under 64 KB.
- CORS is officially "any origin". A preflight I ran today returned 204 with `*` and allowed the Authorization and X-GitHub-Api-Version headers. GitHub's OAuth web endpoints did not return CORS headers, so a browser cannot do the OAuth code exchange without a backend.
- Firebase Auth's GitHub provider can hand back a GitHub OAuth access token (classic scopes; `repo` is broad).
- Cron:
  - The shortest interval is 5 minutes, and runs are delayed under load, especially at the top of the hour.
  - Schedules run on the default branch only.
  - In public repos, scheduled workflows are disabled after 60 days with no repo activity.
  - An IANA `timezone` key was added in March 2026 (I only found secondary sources for this).
- Pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger other workflows. Only `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` are exempt.

6) Secrets
- Each secret can be up to 48 KB, with up to 100 repo secrets and 100 environment secrets.
- Avoid structured data such as JSON as secret values (it can break log redaction). Store the Firebase service-account file base64-encoded.
- Use `gh secret set NAME --repo owner/repo` with stdin, `--body`, `-f .env` or `--env ENV`.
- The USGS M2M `login` endpoint was deprecated on 2025-02-26. Use an application token with `login-token`.

7) Git LFS
- GitHub recommends repos under 1 GB (and strongly under 5 GB). Git warns above 50 MiB, GitHub blocks files over 100 MiB, and browser uploads are capped at 25 MiB.
- LFS on Free/Pro includes 10 GiB storage and 10 GiB bandwidth per month. Downloads by Actions count against the owner's quota. With no payment method, going over disables LFS until the next month.
- Community reports say Pages builds need `checkout` with `lfs: true` to publish real files instead of LFS pointers.
- For about 50 MB, plain git is the right choice; don't use LFS.

Cross-cutting fact: Cloud Storage for Firebase now requires Blaze. Spark projects lost all bucket access from 2026-02-03. So photos and other media cannot go to Firebase Storage without a billing account. They have to stay on GitHub (Pages or repo) or Mapbox, which makes the repo-size and LFS questions directly relevant.

On the relayed user instruction (use our own USGS imagery, not fostulbucuresti's): this mostly affects imagery sourcing, not this area. According to USGS EROS pages, scanning Corona film that has not been scanned yet costs $30 per frame. The order is placed in EarthExplorer, and the user has to buy it themselves. Once the order is fulfilled, the Actions job can download it through M2M with an application token. Public-repo runners now have about 90 GB free, which comfortably fits multi-GB KH-9 and Corona scans. That last point is an inference.
