research.concrete_details:
## 1. jsDelivr

**Engine URLs** (assuming the engine moves to a new repo, e.g. `ventura8/historic-map-engine`; the name is a placeholder):
- Pinned version: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ventura8/historic-map-engine@1.4.2/dist/engine.iife.js`
  - Immutable, cached 1 year.
- Major range: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ventura8/historic-map-engine@1/dist/engine.iife.js`
  - Cached 12 hours at the CDN and 7 days in browsers.
- CSS: `.../@1/dist/engine.css`

**Tags:** `v1.4.2` works; jsDelivr strips the leading `v`. Resolve check: `GET https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/packages/gh/{user}/{repo}/resolved?specifier=1` returns `{version}`.

**Response headers to check:**
- `x-jsd-version`
- `x-jsd-version-type`
- `cache-control`

**Purge (best effort, undocumented):**
- `curl -s https://purge.jsdelivr.net/gh/ventura8/historic-map-engine@1/dist/engine.iife.js`
- Repeat for `@latest` and the css.
- Officially, API access is by email to d@jsdelivr.com. The web tool is https://www.jsdelivr.com/tools/purge.

**Limits:**
- 150 MB per package (repo at that ref).
- 20 MB per GitHub file.
- Soft limits: 10k actively accessed files and 100k files per repo.
- No media hosting.
- Note: `photos/Ferdinand.png` is 29.5 MB, which is over 20 MB.

**Built files must be in the tagged commit:** jsDelivr serves the git tree, so `dist/` has to be committed in the commit the tag points to.

**npm route:**
- URLs: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<pkg>@1/dist/engine.iife.js` or `https://unpkg.com/<pkg>@1/...` (unpkg sends a 302 to the exact version with max-age=60 / s-maxage=300).
- Add `"jsdelivr"` and `"unpkg"` fields to package.json to set the default file.
- Trusted publishing workflow:
```yaml
on: { push: { tags: ['v*'] } }
permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }
jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with: { node-version: 24, registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org' }
      - run: npm i -g npm@latest   # need npm >= 11.5.1 (INFERENCE: Node 24 bundled npm may be older)
      - run: npm ci && npm run build
      - run: npm publish --access public   # provenance automatic for public repo + public pkg
```
- Configure on npmjs.com → package → Trusted publisher with: user `ventura8`, the repo name, workflow filename `publish.yml`, and an optional environment.

## 2. Vite 8 (8.3.4) config
```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
export default defineConfig({
  define: { 'process.env.NODE_ENV': '"production"' }, // lib mode doesn't replace process.env.*
  build: {
    sourcemap: true,
    lib: {
      entry: 'src/index.js',
      name: 'HistoricalMapEngine',            // required for 'iife'
      formats: ['iife', 'es'],
      fileName: (format) => `engine.${format}.js`, // engine.iife.js / engine.es.js
      cssFileName: 'engine',                  // engine.css (else falls back to package.json name)
    },
    rolldownOptions: {                        // Vite 8 name (rollupOptions deprecated)
      external: ['mapbox-gl'],
      output: { globals: { 'mapbox-gl': 'mapboxgl' } },
    },
  },
})
```

**Starter kit `index.html` load order:**
1. `<link href="https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v3.32.0/mapbox-gl.css">`
2. `<script src="https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v3.32.0/mapbox-gl.js">`
3. engine.css
4. engine.iife.js
5. config.js

**Notes:**
- In IIFE, `import.meta.url` becomes `undefined`. Don't build worker or asset URLs from it.
- CSS is not injected automatically; the page needs the `<link>`.
- Default target: chrome111 / edge111 / firefox114 / safari16.4 / ios16.4.
- Firebase: bundle the modular SDK (`firebase/app`, `firebase/firestore` or `firebase/firestore/lite` for the read-only viewer, `firebase/auth` only in the admin bundle). Firebase has no official modular IIFE.
- INFERENCE: build the admin bundle as a separate lib build, because IIFE output is a single chunk.

## 3. GitHub Pages switch
- Current setting: `{"build_type":"legacy","source":{"branch":"master","path":"/"}}`
- Switch command: `gh api --method PUT repos/ventura8/bucurestiuldisparut.github.io/pages -f build_type=workflow`
  - Alternatively: Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
  - Needs a repo admin. A fine-grained PAT needs Administration: write and Pages: write.
  - `configure-pages` with `enablement: true` also works, but needs a PAT (with the repo scope or Pages: write), not GITHUB_TOKEN.

**Workflow:**
```yaml
name: Deploy site
on: { push: { branches: [master] }, workflow_dispatch: {} }
permissions: { contents: read }
concurrency: { group: pages, cancel-in-progress: false }
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v6
      - run: mkdir _site && cp -r index.html config.js photos thumbnails geojson _site/
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with: { path: _site }          # dotfiles excluded unless include-hidden-files: true
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions: { pages: write, id-token: write }
    environment: { name: github-pages, url: '${{ steps.d.outputs.page_url }}' }
    steps:
      - id: d
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
```

**Pages limits:**
- Site 1 GB.
- Deploy timeout 10 minutes.
- Bandwidth soft limit 100 GB/month.
- Artifact: gzip tar under 10 GB, no symlinks.
- Responses send `max-age=600`, `ACAO *`.

## 4. GDAL job
```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      layerId: { type: string, required: true }
      entityId: { type: string, required: true }
jobs:
  process:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04          # pin: ubuntu-latest -> 26.04 between Oct 19 and Nov 19, 2026
    timeout-minutes: 340           # hard cap is 360
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-3.13.3   # ~385MB, GDAL Python incl.
      # options/volumes: [/mnt:/scratch]  # only if extra scratch needed; /mnt sometimes absent (#13587)
    env:
      MAPBOX_SK: ${{ secrets.MAPBOX_SK_TOKEN }}
      USGS_USER: ${{ secrets.USGS_USERNAME }}
      USGS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.USGS_APP_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: df -h / && gdalinfo --version
      - run: |
          echo "$FIREBASE_SA_B64" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/sa.json"
        env: { FIREBASE_SA_B64: '${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SA_B64 }}' }
```

**Runner and GDAL options:**
- Without a container: `sudo apt-get install -y gdal-bin python3-gdal` gives GDAL 3.8.4 on 24.04.
- `jlumbroso/free-disk-space@v2.0.0`: `swap-storage` now defaults to false, and `tool-cache` is renamed `preinstalled-runtimes`.
- Public runner: 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, about 90 GB free on `/` (documented minimum 14 GB).
- `ubuntu-slim` (1 vCPU, 5 GB, 15 minutes) suits tiny jobs such as purge or Firestore polling.

## 5. Dispatch from the admin page (browser)
```js
await fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/ventura8/<repo>/actions/workflows/process.yml/dispatches`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${pat}`, Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
             'X-GitHub-Api-Version': '2026-03-10', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ ref: 'master', inputs: { layerId, entityId } })
}) // 2026-03-10 -> 200 {workflow_run_id, run_url, html_url}; 2022-11-28 -> 204 unless return_run_details:true
```
- Poll the run: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs/{id}` (needs Actions: read).
- Token: a fine-grained PAT limited to this one repo, with Actions: read and write. Store it only in the admin's browser (localStorage), never in Firestore or the code.
- repository_dispatch alternative: `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/dispatches` with `{event_type, client_payload}`. It needs Contents: write, which also allows pushing code, so it is a broader permission.
- Cron fallback:
```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 */1 * * *'   # avoid :00
      timezone: 'Europe/Bucharest'
```
  - Polls a Firestore job queue.
  - Disabled after 60 days of inactivity in a public repo; re-enable with `gh workflow enable <wf>`.
- A job that commits with GITHUB_TOKEN will not trigger the push-based deploy workflow. Call `gh workflow run deploy.yml` (needs `permissions: actions: write`) or deploy in the same workflow.

## 6. Secrets
```sh
gh secret set MAPBOX_SK_TOKEN --repo ventura8/<repo>          # prompts
gh secret set USGS_USERNAME --repo ventura8/<repo> --body "$USGS_USERNAME"
gh secret set USGS_APP_TOKEN --repo ventura8/<repo>           # M2M application token for login-token
base64 -w0 service-account.json | gh secret set FIREBASE_SA_B64 --repo ventura8/<repo>
```
- Limits: 48 KB per secret; 100 repo secrets; 100 environment secrets.
- Naming: letters, digits and `_` only; no leading digit; no `GITHUB_` prefix.
- Fine-grained PAT needed for the REST secrets API: Secrets: write.

## 7. Repo size and LFS
- Current repo: pack 47.17 MiB; `photos/` 46 MB; largest file `Ferdinand.png` 29,537,924 bytes.
- GitHub guidance: under 1 GB ideal; warning at 50 MiB; block at 100 MiB; browser upload 25 MiB.
- LFS free tier: 10 GiB storage and 10 GiB bandwidth per month.
- Migrating to LFS would mean `git lfs migrate import --everything`, which rewrites all commit SHAs.
- Recommendation: no LFS. Recompress or convert `Ferdinand.png` to WebP/AVIF instead.
- Admin photo upload without Firebase Storage: `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/photos/<name>` with base64 content and a fine-grained PAT with Contents: write. Avoid sending it in parallel with delete calls (they conflict).
research.risks_and_unknowns:
- **jsDelivr purge is officially gated.** The README says API access is by email request. The unauthenticated purge.jsdelivr.net/<path> behaviour I observed is undocumented and could change.
  - Disclosure: while probing, I sent one HEAD request to `purge.jsdelivr.net/gh/jquery/jquery@3.6/dist/jquery.min.js`, which may have purged that public alias from jsDelivr's cache. It has no lasting effect, but it was not strictly read-only.
- **Purging doesn't reach browsers.** Range, latest and branch URLs carry `max-age=604800` (7 days) for browsers, so after a release some users may keep the old engine for up to a week. Pin exact versions in starter kits if updates must land immediately.
- **The whole-repo assumption is an inference.** That jsDelivr's 150 MB /gh/ package limit is measured over the whole repo at a ref is not stated outright. Either way, a separate engine repo avoids the question.
- **jsDelivr's hard limits are not stated in the 2026-10-05 Terms.** Only the README gives numbers (150 MB / 20 MB), and they "may be increased on request".
- **Runner disk.** About 90 GB free on public runners is a maintainer statement in an issue, not the documented guarantee (14 GB). Disk allocation has varied before (the 72 vs 145 GB incident), and `/mnt` was sometimes missing (issue #13587).
- **ubuntu-latest migration (Oct 19 to Nov 19, 2026).** It changes the apt GDAL version (3.8.4 → 3.12.2) and other tools. Pin `ubuntu-24.04` or a ghcr GDAL tag.
- **Mixed Python versions.** The ghcr GDAL images now note Python 3.14 for their Ubuntu 26.04 base, so pip installs inside the container may hit PEP 668 (externally-managed-environment). Use a venv with `--system-site-packages` (INFERENCE).
- **Tokens in the browser.** CORS makes direct dispatch from the admin page technically possible, but the PAT sits in the browser. If it leaks, a single-repo token with only Actions read/write can just start workflows.
  - Do not store it in Firestore, even under admin-only rules (INFERENCE).
  - The GitHub token from Firebase Auth's GitHub provider uses classic scopes (`repo` covers all private repos), and Firebase doesn't persist or refresh it.
- **60-day cron disable.** What counts as "repository activity" isn't documented; whether bot commits reset it is unknown. A cron-only design could silently stop.
- **Pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger other workflows.** This is a common pitfall when chaining processing → Pages deploy.
- **Firebase Storage needs Blaze.** It is unavailable on Spark (enforced for existing buckets from 2026-02-03), so media must live on GitHub Pages or Mapbox. Pages' soft limits (1 GB site, 100 GB/month bandwidth) then become the binding limits for ground photos.
  - INFERENCE: a separate media repo with its own Pages site gets its own 1 GB.
- **Timezone key for cron.** Only partly verified: the docs page mentions IANA timezone support, but I couldn't fetch the March 2026 changelog date directly.
- **npm trusted publishing for a new package.** Whether it works before the package exists is not explicit; the docs only say a configuration must complete its first publish within 2 days. An npm account is needed, which the user must create themselves.
- **Mapbox licence.** It restricts use to Mapbox products. Bundling mapbox-gl into a jsDelivr-served engine would redistribute proprietary code (INFERENCE: avoid; load it from api.mapbox.com).
- **USGS purchases.** Per the relayed request to buy imagery from USGS: on-demand scans are $30/frame per the USGS page I found (confirm in EarthExplorer). Purchasing must be done by the user. M2M download permissions and data-download quotas weren't researched here; they belong to the imagery-acquisition area.
- **Firebase 13.0.0 is 4 days old.** Its breaking changes are AI Logic only, but pinning `^12.19` until 13.x settles is lower risk.
research.recommendation:
1. **Split the repos.**
   - Put the engine in a new dedicated public repo, e.g. `ventura8/historic-map-engine` (Vite 8 lib build, IIFE + ES, `engine.css`).
   - Keep the Bucharest city site in this repo as a starter-kit instance (`index.html` + `config.js` + media).
   - Never serve media through jsDelivr: the Terms prohibit media hosting, files are capped at 20 MB, and packages at 150 MB.
2. **Release the engine with semver tags `vX.Y.Z`.**
   - Use a release workflow (`workflow_dispatch` with a version input) that builds, commits `dist/` in a release commit, tags it, and creates an immutable GitHub Release.
   - Starter kits reference `cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ventura8/historic-map-engine@1/dist/engine.iife.js` for automatic minor updates (12 hours at the CDN, up to 7 days in browsers), or an exact version for full stability.
   - After a release, purge `@1`/`@latest` on a best-effort basis via `purge.jsdelivr.net`.
   - Optional later: also publish to npm with trusted publishing (OIDC, automatic provenance). That gives immutable versions and fast unpkg range updates, at the cost of the user setting up an npm account.
3. **Vite.**
   - `external: ['mapbox-gl']` with `globals: { 'mapbox-gl': 'mapboxgl' }`, loading Mapbox GL JS 3.32.0 from api.mapbox.com. This keeps the engine small, avoids the licence question, and lets each city pin its Mapbox version.
   - Bundle modular Firebase: `firestore/lite` in the viewer, full Auth + Firestore in a separate admin bundle.
   - Set `cssFileName` explicitly and define `process.env.NODE_ENV`.
   - Don't rely on `import.meta.url` in IIFE output.
4. **Switch this repo's Pages from legacy to workflow** (`gh api --method PUT .../pages -f build_type=workflow`). Use checkout@v7, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5 and deploy-pages@v5. Keep the site under 1 GB.
5. **Keep plain git; no LFS** for about 50 MB of photos. Recompress `Ferdinand.png` (29.5 MB).
   - Firebase Storage needs Blaze, so ground photos go into the repo and Pages (or a separate media repo with its own Pages site).
   - The admin page can upload them through the Contents API with a Contents: write token, or hand them to an Actions job.
6. **Heavy GDAL processing in GitHub Actions in a public repo** (free, 4 vCPU / 16 GB, about 90 GB free disk in practice, 6-hour job cap):
   - Pin `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` and `container: ghcr.io/osgeo/gdal:ubuntu-small-3.13.3`, with `timeout-minutes` around 340.
   - Add a `df -h` guard step, and `free-disk-space@v2` only if needed.
7. **Trigger jobs from the admin page with `workflow_dispatch`** directly against api.github.com (CORS confirmed).
   - Send `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10` to get `workflow_run_id` back and poll the run.
   - Use a single-repo fine-grained PAT with Actions: read and write, entered by the admin and kept only in browser storage.
   - Prefer this over `repository_dispatch`, which needs Contents: write.
   - Optional fallback: a cron poller on the Firestore queue (keep the 60-day disable in mind).
   - Chain deploys explicitly (`gh workflow run deploy.yml` or a single workflow), because pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger workflows.
8. **Secrets via the `gh` CLI:** `MAPBOX_SK_TOKEN`, `USGS_USERNAME` + `USGS_APP_TOKEN` (M2M `login-token`), and `FIREBASE_SA_B64` (base64-encoded service-account JSON). Optionally scope them to an environment with required reviewers.
9. **Imagery purchases (relayed user request):** buying USGS scans ($30/frame for on-demand scans per USGS) is a manual EarthExplorer step for the user. The Actions pipeline should start after the order is fulfilled, downloading via M2M.

verification.area: delivery (jsDelivr, Vite 8 lib build, GitHub Pages and Actions, dispatch/CORS, secrets, repo size/LFS, Firebase Storage, USGS sourcing impact)

verified.claim: 1. jsDelivr /gh/ accepts exact tags, commit SHAs, branches, semver ranges (@1, @1.2) and @latest. Ranges require valid semver tags, and @latest falls back to the default branch when there are no tags.
verified.source: https://github.com/jsdelivr/jsdelivr (README: ranges and latest 'only works with valid semver versions'; 'Falls back to the repository's default branch if there are no tagged releases')

verified.claim: 2. jsDelivr strips a leading 'v' and leaves prereleases out of ranges and latest (v5.3.8 resolves as 5.3.8; @latest is 5.3.8, not 6.0.0-alpha.1).
verified.correction: Live check today: data.jsdelivr.com lists 6.0.0-alpha.1 as the newest bootstrap version, yet resolved?specifier=latest returns 5.3.8, and the no-version URL serves x-jsd-version 5.3.8. The README itself does not document the 'v' stripping.

verified.claim: 3. README cache times: exact versions and commits effectively forever (1-year headers plus permanent storage); aliases including latest 7 days; branches 12 hours.
verified.correction: The README's '7 days on our CDN' for aliases does not match the live s-maxage=43200 (12 h). The live headers are authoritative for actual behaviour.

verified.claim: 4. Live headers: exact versions send 'public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable'; ranges, @latest and branches send 'public, max-age=604800, s-maxage=43200'.
verified.correction: Reproduced today: bootstrap@5 and @main both returned max-age=604800, s-maxage=43200, and @v5.3.8 returned immutable with 1 year. Note that x-jsd-version-type reads 'version' for range URLs too, and only 'branch' for branches, so it cannot tell you whether a URL was a range.

verified.claim: 5. Packages over 150 MB, or single GitHub files over 20 MB, are not supported by default.
verified.correction: The README quote is exact. The Terms of Use (section 4) also mention hard limits but give no numbers. I did not independently re-verify the 403 message from the Nylas forum.

verified.claim: 6. jsDelivr Terms (effective 2026-10-05) prohibit general-purpose file or media hosting (e.g. image hosting) and set soft limits of 10k actively accessed and 100k total files per GitHub repo.
